title: Great hotel and location
text: From friendly reception staff to a great location, we were surprised at how good this premier inn in. Our family room was a great size and very clean. The bed was super comfy and we thought the breakfast was excellent

title: Great Experience.
text: Good large room and bathroom - 2 queen size bed-room. Modern decor, quality linen and pillows, good coffee machine in room. Very good lunch/dinning rooms and roof top bar. Great location close to tube station, parks for a good early day run and in front of Natl Gallery and close to Bond/Oxford streets commercial areas.

title: Visit to best western best time ever!!
text: My time at this hotel was the best my wife booked this by suprise it was one of the best times of my life. The two gentlemen behind the reception were great and so welcoming. The stay there was great comfortable beds but shame that they never had any parking

title: Don't take this hotel...please...
text: I was reading some reviews and I don't know why I didn't take the advise of others...really, I don't know :-( I don't know how to describe the hotel... Just, don't go... The room was so small that I had to go OVER my girlfriend in order to exit the bed...yes..believe... The double bed had ONLY one side out of the wall...so, each time I/she want to go out the bed, we had to jump over the other. The service...really bad. The people are not friendly and never, I say, NEVER they smile to us. The TV had only 3 chains and no remote control... no way to make understand the receptionist that they shoud check it... The electrical cables (and, believe, I know what I'm talking about) where without protections and were a danger for people. The breakfast machines for bread, coffee...etc, didn't work!!! Well, probably you are reading and thinking that I'm hard with them...but, just before going to the room, read the guest book in the left of the entrance...you will see some "nice" comments that people did before you. If you want to know more about, don't hesitate to contact me.. alfil1313@gmail.com Regards.

title: Convenient, but Cramped
text: The hotel is located very near Paddington Station. Our first room was so small that we had no place for our luggage with equally small bathroom. We were moved to double sized room the next day that had 3 single beds and a small seating area with a table. The bathroom was still small and had a shower instead of the small tub of the first room. Both rooms were equally warm and needed to have the window open to get adequate ventilation and cooling. The street can be noisy, especially a problem for front rooms. The breakfast was a disgrace.

title: Horrific
text: Absolutely terrible room, old, small and dingy. To make matters worse the window is next to the bed and it has an awful draft. Not to mention there is no toilet in the room (it's downstairs) and the shower, which isn't in the room either, has a moist towel on the floor and it has no lock. Definitely should be avoided.

title: Excellent value
text: Right next to the tube. Great value. Efficient check in a machine to save waiting for reception staff. Large beds, great shower. Parking options limited but you don't need car if travelling to central London as tube and train are in your doorstep.

title: Sharp practice on bookings
text: We recently booked accommodation, via Mr & Mrs Smith booking, at the Laslett for later this month, as part of our trip to the UK from Australia, and we were looking forward to staying there. Unfortunately, we have been forced to change our plans and cancel the booking, nearly four weeks in advance of our planned stay. We had paid 100% of the accommodation coast as a deposit and we acknowledge that the booking terms specified that this deposit was not refundable. Accordingly, we acknowledge that the Laslett is within its rights to have refused any refund - but, with no costs incurred and nearly four weeks notice, we think that any fair-minded hotel with its interests in revenue balanced by its interest in the needs of guests would have, without prejudice to their rights, agreed to some refund. A classic case of legal rights being a poor justification for sharp practice. I suppose, if this is how they treat people, we are less likely to have enjoyed our stay than we had hoped to be. I would advise people to avoid this hotel.

title: Hotel with rooms smaller than 8m2
text: Probably the smallest room in the world for 85£/night !!! without breakfast. True, we are in Marble Arch area, but not in the chique part of it though. True, it is 5 min walk from the famous Primark megastore, but that is the only positive note, together with a friendly reception. For the remainder, if you like to sleep in a 8m2 double bedroom WITHOUT toilet nor shower (and like to go upstairs therefore), then this is your pick. For us, never again.

title: Comfort, convenience and value for money
text: This hotel has been fully renovated and is a great place to stay. The day manager was exceptionally friendly and helpful. My stay at the hotel was broken by some time in Paris On my return I was welcomed back like an old friend. It was my first trip to London and he was always very happy to give me really useful advice in relation to getting to various destinations in and out of London. It is so close to the tube station that getting around London was quick and easy. Make sure you get an Oyster card at Heathrow if you are coming to London by air and hop onto the tube which will take you straight to your hotel which is just around the corner. Couldn't be easier. On Earls Court road (just around the corner) there are plenty of shops, a laundry, post office, grocery shops, restaurants, fast food and takeaways - everything you need. The room I had for the first part of my stay was on the first floor and overlooked the Earls Court tube station. I did not find that a problem. The noise of the trains was no more than a low rumble occasionally. I certainly didn't find it disturbing or lose any sleep. When I returned from Paris I was allocated a ground floor room facing the street which was a little more noisy with the sound of people talking as they passed the building. The only thing I would criticise would be the breakfast. Stick to the toast, cereal, juice and coffee. Give the croissant, ham and cheese a miss - it is served on a plate that is straight from the fridge and the croissant is stale and cold. For some people the bathroom may prove a challenge because of the size. It was fine for me (I am on five foot) but I think taller people may find it a bit cramped. If I am in London again the Trebovir will be my hotel of choice.

title: Comfortable, cosy and exquisitely unique London stay
text: Great location, beautiful rooms, charming host. There are only 2 bedrooms, so book well ahead! Its location between 2 tube stations and lines was totally convenient. We could not believe we were in London from our room.

title: Scaring experience
text: I'm used to sleep everywhere, I usually do couchsurfing but I decided to go to London with my boyfriend and we wanted more intimancy. So, the hotel was the worst place to have it. The room was dirty, full of dust on the furnitures and hair on the sheets. The shower was with cold water and the walls were VERY thin. You pay for what you get, but you should have a minimum standard in cleaness!!!

title: Large rooms, don't order Continental breakfast
text: Arrived early at the hotel. Check in time is usually 2pm but room was ready at 1:30pm which was good. They also let you leave your bags at the reception area if you want to walk around before check in time. Bags just lie there in common area relatively unattended so don't leave any important stuff or valuables. The room is big for London. It has a desk, wardrobe, bathtub and coffee & tea. There's no hair dryer so plan ahead if you need one. Also no A/C which would have been appreciated since it was very hot during my stay, but having the window open all day helped cool down the room. Wi-Fi is not good but works to at least get some directions and book attractions. Connection is very slow and intermittent. There are two underground stations that you can use to easily get to the city center. Breakfast is a joke. They still don't know the definition of Continental breakfast so they just leave you there with toast and butter. No meat, no eggs, just plain toast and butter. English breakfast is not that good either. As other reviews said it's served cold, the one egg you get looks like plastic, and taste is not good overall. You're better off going to a supermarket nearby and getting a sandwich with soda. Won't cost you more than 5 pounds and it will be much better than what they give you here. I'd rather have the hotel tell me there's no breakfast included than having to sit there eating toast and butter. I mean just google Continental breakfast people! I have had nothing to eat this morning because of course when they explained that my breakfast was going to be just toast and coffee it was already too late for them to give me English breakfast. The so called kitchen was already closed. Great recipe for a hungry angry tourist, they get that right. Overall the place is passable. Just try to avoid inconveniences and get your breakfast elsewhere. My review is heavily influenced by my hunger right now.

title: Penthouse perfection!
text: The penthouse was spacious and we were a family of 4. Plenty of space with a wrap around terrace. Only issue was check in they are not there 24/7 ensure you have the phone number to call when you are 10-20 minutes away. No early check ins accommodated. There is a waitrose a few steps away and that was extremely convenient. Cleaning is only every few days unless you pay extra. Very modern apartment and I would stay there again in a heartbeat!

title: very disappointing ,travelled 4 london parade.4 2 day trip .
text: 1 good point central location, arrived on friday and had booked group in jan for march 43 people with selection of rooms all of these confirmed by the hotel b4 we left only to arrive and they were nt available totaly different to what was booked . we had 3 married couples 1 single which they tried to put in a room that was as small as hot press in ur hse wit no bathroom , and 3 teens not related to any of them ,when we arrived at hotel there was no rooms 4 them and hotel coulnt understand why they coulnt share and why we couldnt put them in quads when we requested doubles .took 2 hrs to check in 43 people and we had to book theese guests in our group without rooms in another hotel ,totally unacceptable and stressful especially with 22 children wit us all tired and hungry ,manager wd nt see us to sort this out and doesnt wrk sundays so earliest was monday when we wd b leaving this says it all .walls are like paper rooms very small even 4 london.never again stayed in hyde park towers last yr totally diffferent experience wd return there again .

title: Clean up your act
text: I stayed at High Holborn in 429 from August 23rd - left 28th morning. The staff were entirely excellent and helpful, no complaints there. 429 had one operational shower instead of two. One working toilet in stead of two. The kitchen had a large pile of *used* crockery and cutlery piled in one corner which smelt. I though it was disgusting and put me right off even thinking of using the kitchen. Fortunately I found the J D Wetherspoons are good caterers. Breakfast was served on paper plates with plastic cutlery. Are we children? Try cutting a piece of pineapple which is hard, with a bendy plastic knife. What is this doing for your eco credentials LSE? Please wise up and get proper crockery and metal cutlery. Would I recommend this hotel to a friend. Not likely. In the room was ok, beyond that I gave up breakfast by later in the week and stuck with Wetherspoons. I couldn't face that kitchen except to heat water for coffee and feel sorry for the students. LSE, please clean up your act and get green. Otherwise it was fine for the money.

title: Excellent Customer Service
text: I have stayed at multiple Cheval properties over the past few years and my favourite is Thorney Court. I have stayed both as a business traveller and on holidays with my family. On my latest trip the service was excellent as always. The location is great and the apartment sizes and finish are first class. On my previous trip my daughter required a doctor at 2am for an ear infection and the night manager arranged for a doctor to come to the apartment who promptly arrived within an hour. I highly recommend this property.

title: Very noisy, but nice staff.
text: Have stayed here twice so far, both times in an executive room (was upgraded for two nights to a family room, which has two beds in). Firstly the good stuff - nice team here, polite and friendly. Prices are reasonable given that you get a kitchen, living room and as I'm staying here on business it means I could save money by eating in. Location was great for me. The bad side: it's very noisy here. Single glazing means you get a lot of noise from the street. The first time I stayed here the kitchen window wouldn't close properly. The second time I stayed here the room I was in had almost constant music coming from either downstairs or next door - this went on late in to the night, and a door (not sure if part of the property or not) would slam every ten to fifteen minutes and the apartment would shake. This isn't a place to stay if you want a good nights sleep or to relax

title: A very nice stay
text: You just can't do better. Very nice property, great staff and great location. The restaurent was surprisnigly good and good value to boot. We stayed in the smallest room. It was small but really efficiently laid out. This is where I will stay when I come to London.

title: PERFECT, but...
text: This place is IT in London! Great location, beautiful rooms, wonderful concierge services, lovely staff, well-appointed, quiet. Then we checked out... £13 for 2 cups of coffee that we wanted to have in our room (not allowed to just take a cup from the included breakfast

title: Very small room
text: Unfortunately, our room was tiny for a double room, and with the added view of industrial pipes and a wall very close to our window, it was fairly claustrophobic. Staff were friendly and the proximity to London tourist attractions was good.

title: Overnight Stay
text: Great location for business district but also St Pauls and other tourist attractions. The rooms have everything you need and very clean. complimentary tea and coffee in the lounge area and bottled spring water on all the floors

title: Great location but not so great inside!
text: I stayed here only for 2 nights - the first night was better than the first because there was no one else in the rooms around me. The walls here a paper thin - someone opening a can of soda sounded like he was next to me! I chose to stay here because I needed a place with a fridge/kitchenette. No problems there! The fridge, microwave, electric kettle - all good. Even the bathroom, clearly recently remodeled was in good shape - certainly small but fine. If you're particularly tall or larger, though....maybe not the best. The bed was firm and clearly old - I could feel every spring and support in the mattress. My neck will be reminding me all week. The TV is odd - the remote works for the tiny box but you have to turn it on manually....and stand right in front of it to get the remote to work. Annoying but not horrid, The wireless is horrid! Kicks off, takes forever to connect, looses it....you name it. Also, FYI - you need to bring all washing things for dishes - soap, towels etc. There are pots, plates, utensils but make sure to stop around the corner. Distance to Paddington station is ideal - a few blocks down and easy to get to. All in all I'd say if its a quick trip and you really need the kitchen (like me) this is fine but if I had to stay any longer I'd sleep n the floor with ear plugs.

title: An ExCel-ent hotel!
text: A lovely new hotel, spotlessly clean. Really nice room, good size too. Friendly, helpful staff. Good food, but not a big selection. Great value, will definitely stay here again when in the area. Well done!

title: Fantastic
text: Just returned from staying 3 nights at this lovely hotel ... I booked this as a birthday treat for my husband. Checking in was very quick, our room/bathroom was lovely with lots of space. Breakfast was lovely,lots of choice for a full english, if you pre-book this you get a reduction. My husband received a fruit bowl on our first evening and a birthday card from the hotel, which was a lovely touch. The staff could not do enough for you, making sure you had a map,knew which bus/tube you required. The hotel has an enterance into victoria station which is great for access to the train/tube. The location is fantastic, short walk to Buckingham Palace,Westmister,Harrods and lots more. I would use this hotel again on future stays in London.

title: Cosy hotel in Camden
text: We stayed one night at the "York and Albany" with 2 adults and 3 children. We enjoyed it. We had 2 really cosy interconnected rooms (antic furniture ...). Service was very kind and helpful. The situation is almost ideal: near Camden market and Regent's park, 10' from St Pancras Station. Breakfast at the restaurant is really excellent. The best americano in a hotel.

title: Did the job!
text: Stopped there last night as needed a cheap hotel in easy and quick reach of Stamford Bridge. Only a few minutes walk from both Paddington and Lancaster Gate Stations. It was clean and welcoming. That's all I wanted!

title: Friendly staff and centrally located.
text: Very centrally located to the transport in London. Lovely quiet, clean hotel with very friendly and helpful staff members. Not very large room but not tiny either. Has all the usual wants and is very clean, tidy and modern. Free wifi in the room is great. Very short walk to some fantastic eateries, pubs, attractions, convenience stores and cash machines.

title: Absolutely disgusting
text: I stumbled on an offer listed on the Lastminute.com web site during a search for 4 or 5 star hotels for a visit to London for my husband and I and my sister and her husband. The hotel was advertised as a Secret Hotel, luxury 4 star boutique hotel discounted by 45% supposedly. On receipt of our payment we were notified that the Clarendon Hotel, in Bloomsbury was our nominated hotel , on checking the negative reviews on trip advisor we became worried about the hotel. We notified lastminute.com that we were not happy and they asked us to report back following our visit, assuring us that the hotel would be ok. On arrival at the hotel we were checked in and made our way to our rooms and very quickly became very disappointed – the rooms were very small and in no way luxurious. The lace curtains where dirty and hanging down (see pics) The window paint was crumbling and in a terrible state of repair (see pics) The paintwork to the doors was very dirty and dusty and the bathroom door had dirty black hand marks on it – see pictures The wallpaper was very marked - See picture The bathroom was tired, cheaply and badly fitted out- the shower system could in no way be classed as luxurious. I could go on and on about how this room compared so badly to a four star hotel, but I think the pictures say it all. Determined not to spoil our trip away we left our bags and went out to explore London., however I made a quick visit to reception to check that we had been given ‘superior rooms’ and this was confirmed. We returned later that afternoon to quickly get ready for a show we were booked into see to find that a man repairing a window outside our door, on further investigation it was the window from our room which had been removed and was being repaired on the hallway floor directly outside our bedroom (picture enclosed). We only had an hour to freshen up, and had to return to the reception desk to ask that the repair man be removed whilst we used the room. The manager came up to our room, but the repair man was ignoring the manager whom was trying to gather up his tools and move him away from the window and out of the room. Eventually he was ushered out of the room and we began to unpack our things on to the bed – and at this point I cannot stipulate enough our disgust as we noticed the bed spread covering the bed was dirty, and the more we inspected the more stains we found – big black stains (see pic) and even more disgusting white stains all over – a stain every 8” squared. I am sure you can imagine as we did what the stains were, which was enough to make us nearly vomit and to our horror my sister and her husband where identifying the same problem in there room with the bed spread and they equally felt the room was dirty and not luxury four star. My husband asked that the bed spreads be replaced and that the room be cleaned up as there was putty and bits of wood all over the bedroom floor. The house maids then stood outside both rooms repeatedly harassing us for entry to sort the rooms out, again preventing us from getting ready

title: I would NOT stay in this hotel again!
text: Problem 1. Our room card key did not work the first five days of our six-day stay. On the last day someone who was competent listened to our complaint and solved the problem--a bit late, in my opinion. Problem 2. Breakfast was just okay--basic boring ham, musty-tasting rolls. Problem 3. The room was itsy-bitsy. Compliment 1. The hotel was extremely clean. Compliment 2. Location was good--close to St. Pancreas and Kings Cross train and tube stations, and to the Euston, Euston Square, and Warren Street tube stations.

title: Great stay.
text: The staff were all lovely and helpful. The hotel was very clean. We had a drink and a bar snack which were all good and reasonably priced. This was a great hotel for the start of the London to Brighton cycle.

title: Langorf Hotel Frognal Hamstead
text: On Saturday 23rd of May I went to London to see Paul McCartney at the O2 Arena. I stayed at the langorf hotel in frognal, hamstead, which I booked through hotels.com, and got sixty three pounds off the price for one night. The hotel is a great place to stay, i was very impressed, the room was clean and tidy, spacious and had everything you would need, Upon my arrival, I was checked in very quickly and recieved polite and helpful service, The contential breakfast was suberb the next morning, I would highly reccomend this hotel to visitors to London, and hope to return there again. The area round there is very quiet, and in a good area with plenty of shops, it is convienient for the underground and overground with stations located on finchley rd.

title: Good value for location
text: We chose this hotel as it was central and gave us easy access to tube stations and was reasonably priced. The location was excellent with helpful staff, a very comfortable bed and excellent breakfasts. The only complaints we had was the lack of cupboard space and the very small bathrooms with nowhere to put toiletry bags. This wouldn't be a problem for people only staying a night or two. We were however on an extended 8 week holiday, so had two very large suitcases. Julie Australian

title: Sightseeing Trip
text: My son (22) and myself, have just returned from our 3 night stay, we were very pleased with our family room. Separate room for my son, he was very happy. The staff were always pleasant and helpful, room was very clean, comfy beds, tea, coffee, toiletries and ample fluffy towels. Our room was on the front on main road, could be noisy with sirens of ambulances etc but someone needed them. Hotel very convenient to Marble Arch for tour bus routes and Oxford street. Loads to see nearby and great underground and local buses no 6 to Lyceum Theatre. Had a really nice time here, thank you to all the staff for doing a great job, would have no trouble visiting again xx

title: Never again
text: I currently travel to London on a weekly basis and the company I work for normally book me into Hilton/Holiday Inn/Novotel etc. However this particular day London was very busy and the hotel agency could only offer the Langorf Hotel. I looked at their website and tripadvisor and thought it looks ok - it was only for one night. What a mistake!! When I arrived at the hotel I checked in and went to my room which was chinzy but clean, however there was an awful banging noise coming from somewhere so I went to reception and was told it was the boiler which was faulty and suggested I turned the radiator knob down as this might stop it - it didn't. Whilst I was at reception I enquired about an evening meal - the receptionist said they really don't do meals but took me to the kitchen and offered to make me a cheese toastie!! being a female on my own I was very reluctant to find somewhere to eat so I accepted her offer. Could it get any worse?? I was awoken at 1.00am by someone hanging around outside my bedroom door. I phoned reception who came and I heard them ask this man to move and get out!!.After trying to get back to sleep I was then woken by the banging of the boiler again at 5.00am - at this point I decided to get up. I was going to have their continental breakfast but it didn't start til 7.30am so I asked for the bill and went to work early. I would not recommend this hotel.

title: Horrendous!
text: Stayed here and the service was very poor, the sheets were torn. The breakfast was disgusting stale bread to make toast and a nasty yoghurt with water! besides that i left my tablet in the room and they claimed they could not find it until i threatened to inform the police and it miraculously turned up.

title: Not what you see online
text: I just discovered this site while searching for reviews of Italian hotels, and decided to write a review of the Park International. I must agree that the single room was tiny, and not what you expected after seeing the website. This hotel makes a big deal about it's Kensington address, which is convenient, but it does not live up to the upscale reputation the Kensington area has. The room was clean, and the public areas were decent as well. I also had the feeling, as others have mentioned, that they treated me a little less nicely because I had pre-paid through expedia. The front desk staff seemed to be mainly Russian or soemthing, and very very cold, as if a smile would have cracked their faces. All in all, it wasnt bad considering the location, if you won't spend a great deal of time in your room.

title: Cancellation guarantee turns out to be false
text: I made a group booking through Booking.com of almost 5000 GBP with a cancellation/modification guarantee up to a date. The hotel sent me a special contract because of the size of the booking, with an earlier cancellation/modification date. Before this date, I shortened the booking for one of the rooms from 5 to 3 days. It then turned our that the hotel raised the price of the 3 days to a total equal to the original 5 days. When I complained, they said it was an automatic adaptation made by the booking system and they could not do anything about it. They claimed I made a new booking while all that I did was cancel two out of the five days in the booking made and guaranteed to be adaptable. What a despicable attitude towards any client, let alone one with a large volume booking. In addition I had to ask three times for a correct invoice because it kept being incorrect. They had to send it by email because the reception could not access the system. They also did not keep their promise of offering all the rooms on lower floors because there is no elevator. Together with the disappointing quality of the rooms and the breakfast, it turned out to be a very bad experience so I advise everyone to stay away - many better offers in the area.

title: Beware of the big bad manager
text: If you like roughing it, this is the place for you, that is if you like to pay very expensive to go rough. The first look is chic and modern but after the ladies in the reception are done with you, even a scrubby hostel would do just fine. We were greeted by a Russian or Polish girl, well greet is not the correct word. There were some things that were not clear so we tried to ask, but the girl did not know a thing, so another lady approached us and she was so rude and bad-tempered I almost swallowed my tongue, to my shock I found out that the Iranian lady is the manager. We sheltered from her wrath and went for the room. The room was so dirty and the carpet was badly stained, the property not even one year old deserved a makeover. The Monday afternoon, after a hard day touring through London, we retired too the apartments and found a different atmosphere. We were properly greeted by a young South African man

title: Good value and Great Ambiance
text: Staff are friendly and helpful perfect location (5min walk from Oxford St & Oxford Circus tube Station). 20 min walk to London Zoo or British Museum. We stayed in a 4 bed room (bunks) - mattresses on bottom bunks were a bit ordinary as cheap foam and are used as seats if you are in your room. We had our own bathroom which was great. Common area is kept clean and is spacious. Reception open 24 hours for assistance, food and drinks. We didnt find the common room excessively noisey with people checking in and out and gathering together for conversations. Everyone had headphones if listening to devices. One power point in our room did not work. I'd stay here again - just for the friendly staff, service and location. We were in a room on 5th floor with one lift sometimes the wait was a bit long but this was usually during peak periods such as breakfast and dinner times. We just timed our visits to the room during these periods. Quieter on the 5th floor.

title: Never disappoints
text: I always enjoy my stay here. Clean rooms, lovely breakfast and the people working there, as well as Mr Rogers, are always so nice and welcoming. This hotel is about a 5 minute walk from Shepherd's Bush tube station (red line) in less than 15 minutes you're in Oxford Circus. If you prefer the scenic route, I'd recommend taking a bus. It takes longer but so worth to be at the top of a double decker! Already planning my next stay! Thanks so much!

title: 4 days, 3 nights in London
text: Good location. Clean room. Quiet. But poorly equipped. We were two persons with only one set of towels. Basin in the bathroom was very tiny and couldn’t even wash hands properly. There was not even a chair or a small table to put a bottle of water on. We had to place the bottle on the floor. Wall foldable chairs would help in such tiny space. All our stuff were on the floor. Central AC, not such a good idea. No window...if you want one, ask for upgrade but this will cost more. Room cleaning...yes this costs extra too. But anyhow...because of this we spent more time walking around the city!

title: Conference
text: I needed a hotel in london with a conference facility, I spoke to the Manager Christopher, who from the very outset was excellent. The Hotel was a perfect location, the staff couldn't have been more helpful and they made the visit for our group very smooth. We used the pub attached and had breakfast there. I would definitely use this Hotel again.

title: Good Hotel, Restaurant Menu, and Service was Great!
text: Having a Sunday lunch engagement with Mother can sometimes be problematic and expensive a visit to the New Tulse Hill Hotel on a beautiful sunny day was incredibly enjoyable, great service, good menu and a good choice of wine, the venue certainly gets my vote, we will return!

title: A Total Rip Off - Don't Go!!!!
text: I wish I had read all the other reviews before I'd booked this hotel. On arriving, after 10 minutes or so, I discovered the self check in system. Not something that is advised on booking and had it been I definitely would not have booked. Its totally impersonal and the website describes this place as cosy but it is far from that. My room was the basement room. I felt like I'd been put in the dungeon. Immediately on arrival I wanted to complain but as there are no staff at all, there is noone to complain to. A great idea on the hotels part as who can complain if there's noone there? When I got into the room, I discovered is smelt damp, there was no phone signal, the window was open, obviously to get rid of the damp smell, but it was around 2deg outside. The shower, which is described as an ensuite on the website, was the size of a downstairs loo. The shower was worn and the water went from scalding to cold whilst I was under it. The towels, described as white and fluffy on the website, were threadbare. The only positive I can think of was the young girl who helped to clear away breakfast, she was very polite and personable but the only member of staff available and clearly not equipped to deal with the numerous complains she would have received. Overall this place is a rip off at £99 and would advise anyone thinking of staying to avoid it like the plague!

title: Not great
text: I'm used to hostels but this place wasn't great for the price we paid. Even though we paid for a two-person room (bunk bed), we might as well should have stayed in a dorm. Walls were thin, we could not talk in our room because neighbours could hear us. There were no windows in our room and it felt stuffy. I have to say great location and convenient for public transport but that's the only plus point. Just know what you're getting yourself into before booking this hostel.

title: We loved it!
text: Event though we read some bad comments we would like to go to this hotel. We found it great! Really cleaned and well furnished room, staff really kind and gentle. The breakfast was really good. We had no problem with anything. We would return there!

title: An English hotel of distinction
text: A hotel of distinction particularly as regard to service -- the staff across the board was attentive, generous, interested in being hospitable and professional. The hotel excels in its accommodations, its service, its location near two Underground stations. On a scale of 1-5, I give it a 10.

title: Terrible service
text: Despite ringing and booking a month in advance over the phone they booked a single room despite requesting and advising it was a triple room. They were then very unhelpful and refused to address the problem or admit fault. Would never book again.

title: Our overnight stay.
text: Clean comfortable room, very friendly and accommodating staff, nothing was too much trouble. Great location too and very reasonable rate for the area. Free breakfast but alas we missed it (too much of a good night) ! Would definitely recommend and stay again.

title: Adequate
text: We chose this hotel for convenience to Paddington for the Heathrow Express. For that purpose, it got the job done, and its proximity to Hyde Park was a plus as well. Setting on Norfolk Square is lovely. The property itself is just okay. Building is nice on the outside, but not updated or well maintained on the inside. Rooms not quite shabby, but outdated, with plenty of scuffs and scratches. Uncomfortable beds. Breakfast not very good. I think the location is the only reason they are able to get away with the price. Poor value. (We probably paid a premium for a stay just before the new year.) Overall, I was disappointed. Very glad we stayed elsewhere for most of our trip.

title: No sleep!
text: Next to a nightclub, I didn't get to sleep till after 04:00! Sheer torture. Avoid like the plague.

title: Love this place
text: Have stayed here many times and just spent another one night stay. Convenient for the railway and for walking into central London. Clean rooms, good service, great food. Nice to have laundry facilities on site. Pity there is not a spa or gym area but I know they have an affiliation with a local service. Good value for money and always my first choice for accommodation in the city.

title: So Sienna Kilburn
text: We actually booked for the So Sienna apartments in Hammersmith for 3 people. When we arrived the apartment was only large enough for 2 with no cooking facilities. Got moved to Kilburn which was larger. No pots & pans or kettle, fridge didn't work and smelt horrible and beds were terrible. Was very expensive for what we got, disappointing.

title: Absolutely shocking, thieves!!
text: As you can probably tell by my title I'm not happy. When we arrived on the Saturday at around 2:00 pm we were greeted by one of the staff members, who check us in no problem, he then asked for a £10 deposit for the key, which we thought was fair enough, he said we would get it back when we checked out. So we check out on the Sunday morning and the women behind the counter just say thanks that's you all checked out, I then said "you've got our £10 for the key" she says "no there's nothing here" I said "I gave the guy £10 for the key deposit" she doesn't even say sorry, she just says "well if you haven't got a receipt... You should always ask for a receipt" so I'm standing in pure shock! "So your tell me that the other staff member stole my money?" She replies "I'm not saying that, you could be lying to me" Now she's accusing me of lying!!!!!!! It was getting embarrassing for everyone, they were not budging, if I thought it would have helped I would have called the police but for the sake of £10 I couldn't be bothered, it's just the principle!!! Terrible!!!! DO NOT STAY HERE

title: Great location and friendly, helpful staff
text: Stayed Friday evening - arrived late at 10.45pm and collected room key quickly and hassle free from an automated machine (staff were on hand and happy to help if needed). The room was spacious, clean and comfortable with hairdryer included. Staff were very friendly and helpful, particularly at breakfast which was very relaxed and a great start to the day. The hotel is well positioned to the lovely Southbank area of London and is close to a tube station. The hotel would have got an excellent rating had both lifts been working!! I would definitely recommend this hotel and look forward to staying there again.

title: Quick business trip to the City
text: Not impressed with the breakfast service. Got hit with a £5 extra charge for a couple of rashers of bacon with my full breakfast. Very odd and not advised beforehand. Rooms are good albeit breakfast offering lets the side down.

title: Great location and budget hostel
text: Good thing about this hostel was the location,5 min walk to King's Cross station. The private room ensuite was basic and clean. Room had a roof window for some air which has remote control to shut-down. air conditioning and decent size shower and toilet.. Friendly staff and helpful ... Overall the stay was great, only thing I was concerned was to pay £5 to store your luggage for the day. which was bit expensive. where other hostels has free storage facility. There was lot of coffee shops and restaurants near by which is good sign... Free wifi available need to ask for password at reception.

title: No good at all
text: Dirty hotel, the cleaning services were no good at all. The bathroom (through the sewage) was constantly smelling terrible. Breakfast no good. Breakfast time only 7:15-9:15 (not suitable for vacation time). Too noisy. the floors from above along with the water tubes were making too much noise. Check-out at 10:40 (first time I experienced this). Internet only with charge (we new that before we chose the hotel). It was cheap but I WOULD NEVER RECOMMENDED IT, even to my enemies. We had chosen it because it is only 3 minutes walk from the Paddington Station.

title: Sad to leave!
text: I heard about 40 Winks through the Lonely Planet guidebook to London. I was looking for a place in East London that wasn't a big hotel chain and had some personality. After a long day of travel from Madrid, it was so nice to arrive at 40 Winks, which is unlike any place I've stayed before. I had a good chat with David before going out to explore a bit. The accommodations are absolutely stellar. Everywhere you turn there are interesting, beautiful things to look at and admire. Each day I'd notice some new design in the detail of the wallpaper or the way a shadow would fall based on the shape of a lampshade. David was super helpful to recommend good spots around town (for example, Daunt books, which I could have spent all day in!) and I had such a great time talking to him about theatre, culture, politics and all sorts of things. I'm so sad I was only able to stay a couple of nights before flying home. I would love to stay here again in the future and would definitely recommend it to friends.

title: Gainsborough Hotel - Fantastic location for museums, needs refit
text: Our small group, meant we booked three rooms in this hotel a double, twin and single. The entrance to the hotel is well presented with good maintenance unfortunately the rooms are not as good. All three rooms we booked required maintenance attention, with decoration very tired and in room fittings also requiring replacement due to their age. The overall appearance of the rooms was OK but everything was very tired. Definitely not the 4 Star rating that was promised. All our rooms were on the small side especially the single which had only a narrow gap to the side and end of the bed. Rooms are hard to find and have unusual layout to fit them in the building. On opening the door to the twin you are presented with a stair case up to the room with the wardrobe at the bottom of the stairs. None of the rooms had a dedicated space for tea / coffee facilities with the equipment being located in cupboards / wardrobes etc. The Staff were a mixed bag and all bar one we encountered were mixed foreign with less than ideal spoken English, causing confusion and making explaining details in both directions hard. Some of the staff were particularly rude in attitude, however this may have be due to the poor level of their English. The continental breakfast (standard) was OK with no real complaints, albeit a little limited, ham and cheese provided was of poor quality but acceptable. Upgrade to full English cost £5, whether this was worth it is debatable, personally I would say not. The location of this Hotel is excellent if visiting the museums with the Natural History almost literally across the road (2 Minutes) and the others commensurately close. The nearest tube (South Kensington) is about a 5-10 minute walk. Overall the hotel is tired but acceptable, I would rate it high 2 star, definitely not 4 star. I would stay again but not by choice, as it would be quite far down my list. If we had not have got very discounted rates I would have been quite annoyed but for the price we paid and level of accommodation versus the location this was OK, but not much better than OK.

title: QUIET, BOUTIQUE UPSCALE HOTEL
text: On our return second visit to London from Edinburgh, we stayed at this hotel. Our previous London stay was at the St Ermins Hotel in Westminster. The St James is another nice boutique hotel that is in a great location for walking around and enjoying restaurants, shopping, historical sites, etc. It's located down a side street at the end of a cul-de-sac. It's really quiet. We arrived via taxi and were nicely greeted. The front desk/reception area is small, but the staff were very professional. I would be remiss if I didn't mention that the room we had was larger than the St Ermins. The bathroom area was also nicely appointed as well with modern amenities and a nice walk-in shower. We did not feel cramped at all. So, if you are looking for room size, this hotel has it beat over the St Ermins in that respect. We stayed several nights during our second visit and would definitely return. The only meal we experienced there was the breakfast buffet. It was very nice, but the room and variety is smaller than the St Ermins. Again, the front reception staff are quite knowledgeable and helpful with where to go or where to dine. They made a nice recommendation for us on our first night. We wanted to have Italian food and did not want to walk far to get there. They recommended Al Duca and it was a very good choice (more on that in another review). We would definitely return and stay again. Next time we would probably explore the Mayfair and Piccadilly areas more, also within walking distance.

title: Loved it...will return!
text: 3 nights in a double room, most enjoyable! Nottinghill area, apart from the main road, has a lovely village feel. Great restaurants nearby, plus the parks and beautiful shops. It felt much more peaceful than our usual London expierence, but still had the London buzz we both love. Very helpful staff...set us up on Uber which was great, lots of good books, very boutique hotel atmosphere. Only thing missing, for me, tea and coffe making in the room, but everything else made up for it.

title: Stay
text: The block has parking and a day time concierge. It is perfectly located for transport at Tower hill and Aldgate tube stations and the DLR. perfect for Tower Bridge, the Tower, St Catherine's Dock and walking along the river in any direction. Some good pubs but a lot is closed on a Sunday as this is the City not the West End etc. Not many shops in the vacuity but tube rides will get you anywhere you want. It is in the congestion zone area. Several flats are owned, other are rented out for single or multiple nights. The whole block is very warm!! And sits on top of a Tesco and gym.

title: Great budget B&B
text: We had a twin room for 5 days, facing the back yard. Very quiet, even with the window open during the night. Clean room, small but OK bathroom-cabinet. Warm breakfast which was good (compared to other London budget hotels/B&B's), but I missed the bacon! Less than 5 min walk from Paddington Underground, also quite close to Lancaster Gate underground station Friendly and helpful staff/owners. Wouldn't hesitate to book in again.

title: never book with priceline again!
text: in all fairness my issues with this hotel are not the hotels fault per say but I booked a room for my family to visit London when I confirmed on the day that all was fine I was told the hotel didn't have the facity for children to sleep but I could buy an airbed so I wasted half a day trying to do that, when we arrived we were offered no help with the steps (my wife is wheelchair bound and found the corridor was to narrow for a wheelchair so she had to manage while I collapsed the chair to get it in on viewing our room we quickly realised they left no bedding for our children and as the room was tiny (the smallest iv ever stayed in) my 2 children forced to share a single airbed under a table as no room for a second and the bed wasn't a double it was a 3/4 at best so nobody slept

title: Great place to stay
text: Few minutes walk to nearest underground station. 5 minute walk to the tower bridge. Restaurants nearby. Hotel clean. Staff very helpful. Child's bed was a proper bed not a fold up/pull out bed which was good.

title: Stay in Marble Arch Inn
text: Location is very good. But: 1) Room is extremely SMALL and overpriced. 2) Hotel in website mentioned that BB basis, but when you check-in the say that it is only "Bed Basis". 3) I never seen such “small shower”, you hardly move in it, really. 4) Phone in the room doesn’t work if you would like to reach receptionist or in an emergency case. 5) There is almost no space in the room to move. 6) Seems that owner split 1 rooms into 3-4 rooms and re-designed in order to make a revenue. 7) No elevators and so small stairs, you need to carry luggage by yourselves. 8) From room you can hear what is happening in all other rooms and room above. 9) Staff grooming - No Grooming at all 10) Check out time at 11:00am and they start to call you an hour in advance for check out I would never recommend this hotel to anyone!!!

title: London Hilton on Park Lane
text: The hotel was chosen because of its location. The staff were friendly and very helpful from the minute I checked in to the moment I checked out. It's an excellent hotel and good value for money but found bar prices a bit high.

title: Horrendous.... avoid!!!
text: We stayed at the Dylan Apartments on a business trip for 3 nights.... 3 nights too many. Upon arrival the entrance and hallway appear to be quite nice, do not let this deceive you. We were in room 5, it was the dungeon. It was a tiny room in the basement. I could deal with the fact that the room was small as it is London after all but everything that comes with it.... I simply can't deal with..... *it smelled of faeces!!!!! * no windows and a skylight that was cracked. * no ventilation. *the bathroom sink leaked. *the TV remote was broken *One ring of the hob was broken *the toilet flush regularly became stuck and didn't stop running. *the bed creaked every time you moved. It was also uncomfortable with pillows that resembled the roadside kerb. Dirty looking duvet cover. * the walls/ceilings had damp stains *the shower was so small i had to use the toilet seat to put my toiletries on as the space was too small to bend down to pick them up. *broken tile on bathroom floor that had broken to a sharp point and was sticking up. *the walls are very thin so you hear every little noise from other rooms. * night storage heater in room that looked like it had been there since the place was built! *there was a mouse trap in the basement hallway under the radiator. Sure sign of problems. All in all, I'm just reiterating what everyone else is saying. I've stayed in some places before but this is up there with the worst. When you feel you need to go home and disinfect your belongings after staying there there's something not quite right. AVOID AT ALL COSTS!!!!

title: Very good value and safe
text: Great location, great staff, very reasonable rates (plus a reduction for only having 3 in a quad room). Rooms are clean and serviceable. Only one complaint, the fire alarm went off at 6.50 am!! Finally, although it's adequate and surprising that its included considering the low rates, I would recommend going out for breakfast!!

title: Family weekend with outings planned in central London so the hotel is very well placed for that
text: We were disappointed, had been there before but found things rather tired looking this time. There was a smell of drains in our room and a broken toilet seat- worse for the men I am told!!! Breakfast was OK, the restaurant staff were really kind but the food was very expensive, so we went out round the corner the second day. There are good cafes close by. We had what I can only assume was a technical problem with our booking, and ended up having to pay twice for our room. I have not been able to understand exactly why. It made the weekend extremely expensive for me and the attitude to what had happened upset me and coloured my judgement. The front of house management staff said at the time they did not think we would be charged but it needed a senior managers decision. We were told a senior manager would ring on Monday

title: unfriendly staff
text: I was in this hotel with my mom between 19-20.11-13, it is ok if you just want to sleep. Staff was very unfriendly, reception persons tried, but the others...no good morning, no goodbye no nothing and when we try to ask some advise to some place and shop, they criticise our choises and so on..breakfast was ok, but the åerson who worked there...you cannot be and look more unfriendlier, it obviosly was not personal beause they behave like that almost everyone and two ladies table next to us wondered that have they done something wrong because no one didn¨t even say good morning, same to us. I work my self in the customer service and accomodation services and I don´t aloud anyone in our company to bahave like that with customer, unfortunately we felt ourself not wanted.. Room was smelling very damped and we kept windows open almost all the time when we were in the room. I visit London many times a year and have use same price range places and I would not use this hotel twice, places where I have been were fullybooked and i think for reason, this was my moms first trip to London and that is the reason why I am so sad about that, but this is not her last, so better luck next time.

title: A night away in London
text: We were looking for something different and didn't want to stay in a big hotel chain. We like the pub atmosphere and wanted to run up Primrose Hill in the morning. The New Inn ticked all the boxes for us. The welcome we received was warm and friendly and the owner and his staff couldn't have been more helpful. The location was perfect for what we wanted to do and we walked in from and back to Paddington Station. The place was spotless and our evening meal was great. Didn't get time to try the silly hats or the Jazz but next time we will. Thank you for adding to our weekend.

title: A disappointment.
text: I chose this inn for it's location. When approaching the inn, bags of rubbish in black plastic bag was lining the pathment, rubbish collection day, anyway a bad omen. The front of the inn was pretty which was good to see. It was early evening and dark in October, the front door was locked, so I had to ring the bell to gain entre. The inn is 2 adjacent house join together which means narrow staircase, small rooms and shower room more suited to caravan or boat. My room had a wall to wall bed. The pane of glass in the window was too small for the frame, so there was a natural flow of fresh air. The included breakfast was a bun in a plastic bag, portion size cereals and small box of long life milk. I decide to have breakfast at the nearby MacDonald. In short, not worth the money. Better off going to branded budget hotel like Travelodge .. basic, but clean and warm !!!

title: Don't go if you're tall and/or claustrophobic
text: This hotel scarred me. I only stayed for one night, yet my experience there was pretty dire. The staff were fine, accommodating, helpful when needed to be. But the problem is that I'm 6"7. Nothing wrong with that, I hear you say. However, I didn't expect the room I was going to stay was *that* small. The staff member I saw warned me before I was given my key but honestly, I wished I was warned before I booked my room. I was a victim to false advertising. The small room made sleeping a nightmare and there wasn't much walking space because it was covered by my small suitcase I brought with me. The lowlight for me had to be the shower room. I don't suffer from claustrophobia, however, I was very close to suffering from it that one night. The shower room was so small. I slouched all through my cleaning process. And the room was stuffy, no air coming out of the extractor fan. On the bright side, you can have pizza delivered to the hotel...

title: Fantastic guest house!
text: We were delighted that our room (1) was beautiful. Nicely decorated, such a comfy bed, and a sofa, coffee table, desk, chair and wardrobe. The bath has two showers which you could use at the same time

title: Well What Can I Say
text: On arriving at the Grantley, we were showed to our room. It was very small and bathroom even smaller. The toilet being practically on top of the sink, no room to move. The shower was so slow wondered if it was ever going to work. The bed was lumpy and flat pillows with no extra ones if needed. The room was on the main road hence very noisy and single glazed windows, so no sleep the first night. The wall between rooms was so thin that every noise could be heard from the adjoining bathroom and I don't mean the pulling of the flush. On mentioning these things in the morning we were asked what did we want them to do about it (not what I call customer friendly). Yes it is close to the tube station but that is about all that can be said for it. The price you pay is not the quality you get. Somebody needs to take a long hard look at this hotel. At the end of the day not a pleasant experience.

title: Noisy and smallest double room ever.
text: The rooms at the first floor at the front of this hotel are noisy and tiny. The Seven Sisters Road is constantly busy and the "double" bed is forced under the window with your head next to the window. Even with earplugs and windows closed the traffic is noisy. The room was described as a double room, at best it was a large single with a double bed crammed in . No fans in the heat, 1 double socket so far away from the bed making it a pain for phone alarm etc. Was also a little disturbed by the request to photocopy my driving licence ... The room had been pre paid by our agency and I had shown positive ID . Letting someone take a copy of personally identifiable data seemed unreasonable. I would never stay here again I'm afraid .

title: Do not stay here under any circumstances!!!!!
text: As I am writing this I am currently in the process of suing the apartments for unauthorised debits to my account and misrepresentation of copy on their web-site. We stayed here some 4 weeks ago for two nights as we had organised a large fundraising night for cancer research and wanted to stay near the venue. We arrived later than expected due to traffic and had been told by friends staying at the apartment that they had been turned away even though they had a confirmed booking due to essential maintenance work. We had booked a family room and an executive room. Upon arrival, we realised that both my parents who are registered as disabled would not be able to stay as the apartments have no lifts and huge staircases. We were shown to our "family room" which meant climbing a very tall spiral staircase to find a room in the eaves with a lumpy mattress and a second bed under the eaves that you had to climb into backwards. There was a small shower room and worst of all only a sky light measuring 1 foot by 2 feet with no way to reach this to open or close it. It was in effect like being in an underground bunker. We are still trying to get back the money that we have been overcharged and even with email proof they are still refusing to refund us. Please also be careful as we had a total of 5 friends stay here on the night of our fundraising event and NONE of the rooms matched the size or style of those shown on the web-site. I normally read trip advisor before booking anywhere but made the mistake of not doing this. I am sure that the good reviews come from those that manage to get the rooms shown on the website but to me you are better staying in Fraser Apartments as they are great and you get what you see in the pictures. The management have the Customer Service skills of cockroaches. Be warned!

title: As always, first class
text: Why stay anywhere else in London? Great staff, lovely food and a pleasant ambience. It feels like home, warm and comfortable. Parking in Addington Street a 5 minute walk away and only £20 for 24 hours (this is value in London).

title: A hotel that bends over backwards...
text: My new wife and I spent our wedding night at OneSixTwo after our wedding. It might seem an unconventional choice for a wedding night but our wedding was filmed for a reality TV show in the local area and we wanted something different for us and our guests. We virtually took over the hotel with 8 of the 10 rooms being taken up by wedding guests and from the second we arrived (a very late check in of midnight!) to the second we left (a generously offered extended check out) we were treated like royalty. Breakfast in bed offers (and an extended breakfast time), rose petals on our bed, the extended check out were all things we wouldn't have expected. Dawn, who was amazing, even gave us a wedding card and was helpful and polite throughout. If you're staying in London, and want a stay in a contemporary, comfortable and relaxed environment we seriously cannot recommend this place any higher. Fabulous!

title: Nide hotel in convenient location
text: Near to Earls Court Tube station, restaurants etc. My room on the top floor had no window but a skylight. Quite OK. Staff was friendly and breakfast perfectly OK. Pleasant stay for one night only, in and out from Heathrow and a short visit to a bookshop! Will be back.

title: Disappointing and rather poor
text: The website mafe it look quite promising but the hotel is only mediocre, if even. The staff is rather uninterested in servicing. We had an extra bed in, and the mattress was completely inappropriate for use: That is just the way it is, said the concierge. I guess he was just right...

title: Grim and extortionate
text: The room was tired and old with marked, scuffed and jaded decoration. There was a stale, unclean odour that remained even with the air conditioning turned on and a soiled smell in the bed. The air conditioning turned itself off completely after a short while meaning it had to be continually reset. The windows could not be opened, however the room was on the 1st level overlooking a gloomy enclosed courtyard of loading bays filled with rubbish bins, cars and work people coming and going. Noise started at around 5:am with things being shifted and banged about. The window overlooking this area was filthy, adding to the depressing outlook, but the curtains had to be kept shut anyway as it was opposite offices which looked directly into the room. The bed was nothing like the advertising promised - hard and worn out with no give at all, in fact painful to sleep on. The double bed was made up of 2 single mattresses which meant there was a hard ridge down the middle and sleep for the 2 nights was very uncomfortable. One of the worst beds I have ever tried to sleep on. The bathroom fittings looked clean but the room smelt stale and used with brown and orange stains around the bottom of the shower and shower curtains. The shower was feeble though the water was hot enough. The check in process was marred when our booking could not be found and then both mine and my colleague's credit cards were declined by a fault in the system, meaning we had to be checked in by the reception staff which was awkward in front of a queue of other guests. We had booked 2 rooms for 2 nights and the experience in the other room was not much better. At £200.00 per night each, the rooms are scandalously overpriced and the hotel experience was completely misrepresented by the advertising. My 'overall thoughts' are Grim and Extortionate. To add insult to injury I expect that no action will be taken as a result of my feedback.

title: Great Accommodation
text: Would stay at this place again. Excellent location, great restaurants in the area. We had a shared toilet, but our own shower and hand basin. In the week we stayed there I never saw anyone else going to the toilets, so just trotted down in my nightie. The managers were very helpful and the breakfast was fine. Very good value for money.

title: Not Great
text: I stay in hotels semi-regularly for my work, and this was one of the more poor I have stayed in. The hotel seems clean at first but after spending some time there it became clear that it was not. The hotel was very strongly scented by a plug in which was very over powering. The room was invaded by small insects on the windowsill. The television was not tuned in and a security lock on the ability to tune it in myself, and there was some sticky black substance on the blinds. The beds were hard and the single pillow provided was flat and had a crease in the middle where it had spent time folded in half. There was no cleaning of the room at any point during my stay, some one came in to top up the coffee/tea but no-one made the bed, or cleaned the bathroom/replaced towels. The staff were not accommodating to our request to take breakfast a little earlier due to work commitments. The need to hand your key in every time you leave feels somewhat limiting, though I can understand that this is necessary for security. It is in a convenient location, near to several shops and food outlets, as well as Finsbury Park underground. Overall, my stay at this hotel was not a comfortable one, and I couldn’t give any more than 2 stars for my experience.

title: Basic but great value for money.
text: No frills here but basic, great budget accommodation. Very useful to have a kitchen available. Great location. Excellent transport links and a very handy supermarket a few yards away. Willd definitely book again.

title: poor and tired
text: for my pounds I was expecting more.The room looked fatigued and tired and uncared for It was minuscule, next to the elevator. The only things opulent was the mini bar which did not interest me whatsoever. The mattress had springs I could feel so I had to use the coverlet as a blanket since there was no extra blanket in the room as there was no space to put it, it was that tiny. The entrance looked good and the staff was friendly but a good inviting night they do not make. I felt short changed for my 124 pouns.

title: Great for short or long stays
text: We are very happy that friends recommended this full service apartment/hotel for our nine day stay in in London during September 2012. Our one bedroom unit included a dining room, living room with work table in an alcove at the end, kitchen and two bathrooms. We were on the bottom floor and had a large garden seating area accessible either from the living room or kitchen. The kitchen was fully furnished with everything we needed including a combined washer/dryer. Having the kitchen made breakfast easy. We purchased breakfast and snack items at the M&S around the corner and the Sainsbury across Brompton Road. Our daughter lives south of London used the kitchen to cook six of us a wonderful salmon dinner one night, and the maids cleaned up after us! I found that I needed to keep the front and back windows open at night to cool the unit to my favorite sleeping temperature. Also housekeeping provided a memory foam mattress top that made my wife’s nights more comfortable. The location is a couple of minutes from the Knightsbridge tube station and Harrods. Parks and Buckingham palace are just short walks away. The front desk staff could not have been more friendly and helpful. We found all their recommendations to be excellent, wether for coffee, a great local wine shop, or restaurants.

title: Thank you
text: I checked in here at 1015 at night having checked out of a terrible hotel not far away. Welcomed warmly and checked in quickly. Soon in room and settled. Perfect in every way. Quiet, cool and relaxing. Staff friendly and helpful.

title: Awful don’t bother !
text: Booked for a weekend in London with my boyfriend as we were planning a few trips to the theatre . The only good thing about this hotel is the staff and the location The staff were really professional and very friendly The location is short walking distance to plenty of theatres and great restaurants. However the room was so dated , the bathroom Was tiny and absolutely awful . The bath had a sort of weird box screen around it which made you feel like you were in a box ! It was so small you bashed yourself into it everytime you went in! The room smelt like an old people’s home and was so much smaller than on pictures! The tea and coffee cupboard stunk of must so we didn’t bother having them! At night it was around 7 degrees C and we had the window open all night it was that hot with no control over the temperature of the room ! I get this is a cheaper hotel for the area but it’s still Over £120 a night - and it is most definitely Not a four star !!! This hotel is most suitable For cheap business trips in cold Weather !

title: Too hot and get the decorators in.
text: We stayed here due to its proximity to Hyde Park and Kensington Gardens as we were attending the BST music festival. It was very handily placed in that respect. It was also handy for the shops, bars and eating places on Queensway where there are also two subway stations On the plus side the staff that I encountered were friendly and helpful where they could be except for when we asked for morning call which never came, fortunately we had woken in time but in pools of perspiration and were wringing our pillows out. After seeing photos on review sites I feared the worst. We had room 204 at the front on the second floor. It had double opening bay windows but you had to stand on the bed and reach over the headboard to open them. The weather was very hot but it was impossible to sleep with windows open due to outside noise, a fan would have helped as there is never going to be air con. Our room was at least cleanish with a decent sized bed and just enough room to swing a cat without bashing its brains in on the walls. The carpet had a few marks but nothing too suspicious. We also had a spiders web on the corner of the front and side walls which was there for the whole of our stay, perhaps it was a permanent resident with immunity from a duster. There was what appeared to be newly tiled bathroom with a good shower, new sink and loo but that had to be sat on sideways due to a large towel rail. There is practically no wardrobe space just a small rail with 3 hangers. There is a kettle and tea and coffee things and a small TV. The breakfast was cereal or toast in an inadequate basement dining room. The self service area was in the worst possible place and needs moving next to the small kitchen. The seating is woefully inadequate when everyone descends on it. I know that these places get a lot of traffic but it needs an urgent overhaul in decorating and re-carpeting in the corridors and please discard the filthy settee in reception. I doubt that I would ever return.

title: Bon Appetite
text: Pay attention - It's no worse than any other part of London - and is literally a 60second walk from Tottenham Hale Underground (or overground) station. You are 4!stops away from Kings Cross station (8minutes travel time) with direct connections to every part of London and the rooms are a fraction of the price...8 minutes !!! The restaurant, reception and rooms are quality. Great deal regarding breakfast with 15's and under eating free and the option to get a two course dinner for £16 Bargain (Car park is off site...2 minute drive away, 5 minute walk back. 24hr security though, the Irish manager sold it well so he did..) Picture view from station

title: Good location, clean and comfortable
text: Stayed one night on Mon 13th April 2015 and chose it for location. Staff were very welcoming and although there is no lift they offered to carry our bags. Room was very clean and comfortable. Breakfast room was well managed and staff were friendly and quick to clear away and replenish the cereals/milk/toast etc. It was very helpful that when we checked out we were able to leave our luggage to collect later. Would be more than happy to stay there again.

title: Sadest hotel I ever stayed at
text: Anywhere in North America this would be a $49.00 room. Here's why: -Deadbeat staff except for a few of the underlings who serve at the buffet breakfast. -Creepy doorman who checks your valid breakfast paper (we called him the Undertaker) got into a nasty verbal spat with a female breakfast server right behind us. -male bartender from perhaps Malaysia should not be working around people, he might make a good garbage collector. Just for asking for a sample taste of a beer it was like I'd asked him for his right arm. -worst beds ever with maybe 1/8 of an inch of cloth (no padding) between you and the bedsprings. I got to know each coil spring intimately each night, barely slept 2 hours each night. -bathroom has no shampoo, no facecloths, no hair dryer, the bathroom air vent system doesn't work. Bathub is 2 ft high and very narrow - definitely unsafe for any older or slightly artthritic or disabled persons. -bathroom sink has old style separate faucets for hot & cold meaning to wash you face you have to fill the sink and then clean it afterwards to get rid of the soap scum. -to use their phone (which did not work properly) you have to give a 20 pound deposit - everyone is considered a potential thief here. - room was not attended to until the 3rd day there. They just left new towels and removed old ones. -no kleenex provided -no alarm clock/radio -back side room was quiet other than hum of HVAC system outside. -new window was good and could be opened to refresh room -breakfast was OK but ham slices were the saltiest ever. Don't stay here. There must be better places. -

title: Terrible Stay
text: The rooms are tiny, the air conditioning didn't work. I complained to reception that something had been taken from my room when it had been cleaned and they said someone would come back me but they never did. You can't even say it's good value for money because the price I paid for 3 nights and the rooms you get just aren't even comparable!

title: Very good Hotel
text: I was last November in London in business and stayed in this hotel. It was very good for my needs, clean and professional team made my stay very comfortable. The breakfast was good, but the dinner could be better. I will use it again for sure.

title: Easy hotel and central
text: We stayed for one night in a 5 person room. Size was good, beds comfy, bathroom modern and clean. Great location and cheap cafe around the corner for breakfast. Paid £30 each which for London central is good! Would stay again. Only thing was room was a little warm even with a fan!

title: Beware- They didn't honour our booking , and rude attitude
text: I booked 2 rooms in February through booking.com as 4 of us were going to see the Killers in Hyde Park. We arrived at 1pm to be told we didn't have a booking but after showing our confirmation email and insisting they rang booking.com the story changed. Eventually, acknowledging that booking.com had sent through the details we were told there was nothing they could do with a very unhelpful tone and no hint of an apology. Unfortunately I couldn't get reception to ring booking.com so we had to stand our ground as we had travelled to London by train and you can't bring cases to Hyde Park. Eventually after some conversations they had between themselves in Spanish a lady (again saying what can we do and me saying that is not my problem, they have failed in their contract) brought us across to another hotel where we were told our only option is for all 4 of us to share 1 room. What could we do but accept it. As it turned out the Albro Hotel across the way was spotlessly clean with a lovely breakfast. Needless to say we didn't get to stay here but I would not recommend this Hotel by virtue of their attitude to their mistake. Go to the Albro Hotel across the road where Dave will look after you.

title: Xmas shopping trip
text: Nice hotel in great location just a 5 min walk from tube station ( old street station, northern line ) great bars and restaurants in the area...... well worth a visit. Shoreditch within 5 minute walk. Car park available if needed, good breakfast and very comfy beds.

title: Service, safety and central
text: I first came in contact with hotel owners through their small, budget but excellent restaurant Mandalay on Edgeware Rd. Since then I have stayed at Mandalay Picton House Hotel several times and have always been satisfied. The small rooms and lack of lift are more than compensated for by the first class service and location. The breakfast is hearty, if somewhat greasy, and clean towels are provided daily. I have always felt very safe and comfortable at this friendly, quiet family hotel. Colleen

title: Design without Substance
text: We were very pleased to see that a new, much needed hotel had opened in Notting Hill. Even better it was positioned as luxury in many trusted travel sources. The location is ideal, close to the tube, cafes and the crazy scene found in NH but the hotel is tucked away within Pembridge Gardens and remains rather quiet and unobtrusive. The outside of hotel makes it look fun, with a lovely terrace where guests (and others) can take a drink and enjoy some downtime. The lobby is designed with a small eating area on one side and a bar/lounging area on the other. Both these spaces rest adjacent to a long "bar" which includes the front desk, and an actual bar where a breakfast buffet is served each morning. Our room looked very good upon arrival- large, very clean, king bed, separate dressing area with desk/vanity on one side and a bathroom with large shower on the other. However, once the front desk clerk left me to actually stay and use the room all the delight of the superficial design began to strip away. The room was very noisy being located next to a fire door and on the lower (yes, lower) ground floor. Though it was not street noise, it was guest and staff noise that startled me both day and night-also the smell of food from kitchens or some type of service space. Next, the bathroom was verging on the ridiculous. The super small sink- about the size of a medium salad bowl, and I do not exaggerate, came up to my thighs. I was not quite sure what anyone was thinking, or not thinking, to place such an absurd and useless sink in a hotel. There was no space for toiletry bags or any products let alone to really use this tiny object with any grace or elegance. The shower was not separated by anything but an L-shaped curtain that kept the water around you and worked relatively well. However, the bathmat was placed inside this area which I managed to drench immediately, and there was only tepid warm water- despite best efforts we could not get it hot....which was very annoying. Also much to my dismay, we received a knock on the door by housekeeping at 10am....really? In this day and age, can there be a little more sensitivity to guests in a room on a Sunday morning-figure out a way to train staff to be more aware. The staff was nice but never really looked at you. We left the hotel several times and were barely acknowledged. In the morning during breakfast it was even more of the same. Inconsistent, understaffed and you felt like the staff thought they were doing you a favor when serving you. There was nothing gracious, friendly or warm in any interaction (though front desk staff upon check in was very nice). I would describe it as a certain distance that seemed to be kept between staff and guest. It is understandable if you are staying a a truly groovy hotel with a scene- maybe in Miami at the Delano or Setai, but here? Not expected, not appreciated and not worth it. I did complain to the front desk and requested a room on a different floor. The hotel was full and they could not accommodate a change. I was offered a complimentary breakfast. Upon check out, I told the staff that we had no hot water and housekeeping knocked on the door to our annoyance. Her response was to apologize and asked if I received the complimentary breakfast....kind of clueless response. Hot water is a pretty basic requirement in any hotel, but it was not acknowledged as such-- as I said this distance between staff and guest was fascinating. Overall, if staying at The Laslett set expectations. You have almost no choice in Notting Hill or Bayswater for a decent hotel. Defining the hotel as "luxury" may be a relative term when comparing to other hotels in the immediate area but is truly an exaggeration for the initiated. Despite wanting to love this hotel and return again and again, I say with much sadness that I would never return nor recommend.

title: Aware of Bed Bugs
text: We stayed in this hotel for 11 nights in a triple room . Every thing is going well until the 10th day of our stay, red spots were visible all over our body. Yes, we did complaint to the hotel that they might be ants or bedbugs in our beds.
