First hotel staffs refused about any ants or bedbugs in their hotel until we show our red spots as the proof to them, They promised to do deep cleaning during daytime while we were going out of town. When we came back at night, our room was clean and smell good so we went back to sleep. The next morning we found alive bedbugs on our bed sheets and pillows. Do not recommended this hotel to anyone. We are every disappointed and suffer from terrible itchy.

title: Not a four star hotel by any standards
text: Okay the location is fantastic, the service is fare, the concierge is very good. BUT. The rooms are very small, the breakfast is limited to same options everyday. The dining room is in the basement and is very small. Surprisingly, this hotel has an Indian theme, it should be an international Hilton. The art work is good, but I did not like the smoke sticks they light at the entrance every night, its smill is very strong. Also they put us in a room next to a small housekeeping storage room, every now and then there is someone talking or making noise in the room, I found it hard to take a nap during day time. The price is really too much for the hotel. You better off paying similar rates at better hotels in the same area. Also the room carpet was very dark and filthy. It is late 2013 and still there is no free Internet in the room, there is a sharge of £10 / 24 hours.

title: Worst Hotel we have EVER stayed at !!!!!
text: Worst Hotel EVER !!! no parking and was directed to a pub car park over half a mile away. Booked a twin room and was given a double would not change it. Then insisted we had to pay a £30 deposit for the room even though the company had already paid in advance. Food served until 10.30pm but kitchen closed at 9.50pm when we tried to order !!! Dirty rooms, Terrible rude staff especially on reception. STAY AWAY, YOU HAVE BEEN WARNED

title: Great Location
text: I had a single room which was of a good size, it was clean and comfortable with shared bathroom facilities. It is situated in a quit street and although under the flight path, I didn't notice any noise despite the window being open. The location was great only a 10 minute walk from Ealing Broadway rail and Tube station. It was also handy for the local pubs and cafes etc and the local shopping centre.

title: London break
text: Nice hotel, well maintained and great service, comfy bed which is good for back issues. Staff are friendly and happy to help you with anything. If you want to stay in central London and not spend the earth this place is great.

title: I forgot my iPad in the room and cannot get it back!!!!
text: I have been stayed in the hotel, room no. 002, during 5th - 7th Mar and I found out that I forget my iPad in the room after we checked out. On 7th Mar evening, I called the hotel many times, first time to check if there's anything found in the room - the answer is the housekeeper is out so she asked me to call again tomorrow, second time which I'm sure that my iPad was left there (using find my iphone application) - the answer is nothing was found. So, my iPad was lost in the hotel and I cannot get it back. It's really terrible to face this issue during my holidays. I won't stay in Accor hotels anymore and sure to tell all of my friends about this!!!!

title: Not a great experience
text: First impressions from the website and front reception - great. It went down hill when I left the reception to go to the room. In need of a good paint was the first impressions before getting to the room. Room was small but adequate. Bed had collapsed on one side so spent most of the night trying not to fall out of the double bed. Noise from next door at 4 am didn't help! Sink had no plug so not much use to someone who has a wet shave - managed just. Breakfast was toast and cereals - adequate but what happened to a offer of a full English Breakfast ? Maybe I ask for too much ...

title: Avoid!!!
text: Appalling customer service... I wish I never booked this hotel! Any reputable agency - online of offline should think twice before doing business with Dylan house (London). Hopefully sooner or later they will realize and stop dealing with them. The only reason I booked 2 nights at this hotel via www.bookings.com was close proximity to where I needed to be in London last weekend of October for my NLP seminar. I was called from the hotel only 3 days before arrival date to be informed that they had some maintenance work going on and no rooms were available. Nobody bothered to apologize for inconvenience. I had to find another hotel nearby. A month later while checking my credit card statement I realized that Dylan House still charged me £77 - one nights fee. When I phoned to inquire about the charge, both - bookings.com and Dylan House replied, that this was a cancellation fee for no show.... Please, be aware and try to avoid this hotel at all cost!

title: very good hotel, perfect location
text: I stayed at the Shakespeare for a second year in a row for 22 nights in February. From check in to check out, I never had any problems. Like last year I based myself at Paddington and did day trips out of London using BritRail. Nice hotel, literally a minute from Paddington station and heaps of food places, wonderful view of Norfolk Square, and to top it all, it snowed on my last day there. Will return again next year, thanks Shakespeare.

title: Disappointing
text: What a shame. We wanted to take my mother for Sunday lunch and I happened across the York & Albany knowing it was Gordon Ramsey the food should be excellent having been to the Maze, Savoy grill room and others. I am sorry it was OK but tough beef is not good. The limited roast selection was disappointing so we left after the main dish to get desert somewhere else. Maybe an off day but once is enough. We loved the atmosphere and decor. Pitty!

title: Don't Stay Here - You'll Be Scarred For Life - Literally!
text: I stayed here for one night - Saturday 9th August 2014. I was bitten by bed bugs - 29 times!! We had a night in London and when I woke the next day I found a few bites on my leg, thought they were mozzie bites from the night before - we paid extra to have a window in our hotel room, but the window didn't open so the "mozzie" couldn't have come in from the window. The room was so hot, told the reception who said they would change the aircon - they didn't. Anyway, on the journey home I was becoming aware of more bites and when I got home I found I was covered in them - my back,legs, arms, hands and face. The bites were swelling and very painful, not how I react to mozzie bites at all. I couldn't sleep that night because of the pain and went to the doctors the next day. I tried going to work but driving was very difficult because of the bites on my leg. I had to buy a bag of ice to sit down! My work sent me home and I had to stay there for the week as I felt so awful, and by this time the bites had blistered and I couldn't even wear shoes. I contacted EasyHotel on Monday 11th August by email as there was no phone number to be found. I got an acknowledgement email and then nothing more. I chased them again about 10 days later and have still been ignored. The bites have just about healed now but I have a constant reminder not to stay at this hotel as I have 29 scars to remind me. I am disgusted by what happened to me when I stayed here, and disgusted by the fact that they have ignored me.

title: Anniversary Break
text: What a great place to stay. Comfortable rooms and bed, well equipped bathroom with fantastic shower. The restaurant did top notch food very well presented by very friendly staff, who clearly know how to look after their customers. A 2 minute walk to the train station and then just 15 minutes to London Bridge. Tulse Hill Hotel is a handy place to stay, far enough from the city to be away from the bustle but close enough to be convenient. And if you drive there (like us) there is secure free parking. Not many places boast that these days!!

title: Wouldn't recommend
text: Arrived on the Saturday morning, paid a surcharge of £20 to check in early. Room was clean with the following amenities: - Kettle - Ironing Board (No iron) - Hanger for clothes - Safe However, went to make a coffee only to find the UHT milk was off. There is a large mirror, but no plug nearby to use hair straighteners. Definitely not a power shower! There is no tube station nearby so it's a good 20 minute walk to the 'Tourist' area, this is definitely not recommended in the evening especially with children as this is not the nicest area. However, there is a bus stop very close to the hotel. On the whole it wasn't an unpleasant experience, but not somewhere I would stay again.

title: value for money
text: 70 pounds/night for a 5 persons room inc. breakfast is a very reasonable price for a hotel especially in London. Just about 3 mins walking distance to Paddington Tube Sta. Definately will stay in this hotel again...

title: Great apartments
text: First point is that a lot of folk complain about the location and getting to the hotel. It's a lot easier than many people make it as the hotel is only five minutes walk from the Jubilee Line at Canary Wharf taking you to and from central London very quickly. It's much easier than using the DLR. The apartments are separate from the Marriott hotel although they share a reception. The apartments are a good size with separate living room/kitchen and bedroom with a hallway linking them. Off the hallway is the bathroom. The kitchen is fine with a full size fridge, cooker, hob, microwave and dishwasher. Utensils and crockery are basic but meet most needs. There are washing machines and driers on several floors which are free to use and there's a decent gym. Staff are friendly and the hotel was very clean. All in all a great stay in a great apartment. The location is fine too with some decent local shops and restaurants.

title: When are you coming back to give me my keys for the room ?
text: I stay at this hotel once about 4 years ago . At 1st it was ok . We stay in room number 2 at the bottom floor with a en suite bathroom . The room was old with the owner friend bed bugs . An old TV and a little dark room . As this hotel is close to brent cross and it near the word cheap 60 pound ( but not worth the 60 pound) an emergency happen where we had to stay again .At around 8pm I rang the bell no one answer so I rang again still no answer then a tired old man open the door and shout what do you want . I looked up thinking I was in the wrong place . This man was so RUDE ! I asked if they was any rooms left he said yes and he walked off . I am still waiting for him to come back ! Please you need to close this place down

title: Lovely Place - Great Location
text: We spent 2 nights at the Norfolk Towers in November, and really enjoyed it! It is a clean, comfortable, and quiet place to rest after long days of seeing the sights in London. The desk staff and concierge were very helpful. Value of price paid was very good. I would definitely stay here again!

title: Nice place, great food.
text: We booked this hotel for a family visit to London . There were 7 of us altogether. We had four rooms all of which were very nicely decorated. Our daughters shared a room on the ground floor which was the largest of the four rooms. It was very spacious with a nice sized bathroom and lovely comfortable bed, the down side was that the window looked out on the passage way to the other bedrooms and was very near the kitchen so was quite noisy if you had the window open and quite dark. The other 3 rooms were all smaller but lighter, big enough but with very small bathrooms with inadequate lighting. The towel rails were on the wall above the loo resulting in one towel ending up the the loo during the course of the weekend! The beds in those rooms were a disappointment. They were wooden frames with very firm mattresses meaning they were not comfortable to sleep on. The mattresses didn't fit the frames properly and the framing at the end of the bed was covered with a throw, which looked nice but because you couldn't see the bed frame which stuck out quite a long way, at least 2 of us bumped in to the frames ending up with large bruises on our legs.The rooms were very warm. In the two rooms upstairs we were able to leave the windows open at night which helped but downstairs we didn't like to as it didn't feel safe, especially as one was accessible from the carpark. In all the rooms, even the upstairs rooms it could be quite noisy, mainly from the kitchen/waiting staff, I don't think they realised quite how the noise traveled. On the upside, the food was fantastic! We had a beautiful 3 course meal on the Friday evening when we got there, everything was perfect, not a single complaint, which is unusual for us! The cooked breakfast was very good too, the only disappointment was the price we had to pay for it. We knew there was a supplement for a Full English breakfast but when we came to pay the bill it was more than we had been expecting (although this was rectified), but not as much as the full price on the menu, however, if you had any other cooked breakfast you were charged full menu prices rather than just a supplement which we doesn't seem fair. Don't get me wrong, we enjoyed our stay, the staff were lovely and very helpful, it is a lovely place in a lovely area and the food (however much we were charged) was beautiful. We would recommend it to friends and family but would warn them about the beds and the overpriced breakfast!

title: Small rooms
text: Having read some of the reviews I thought this hotel would be OK as it is fairly close to Covent Garden. I wasn't prepared for how small the rooms actually are. It may be ok if you are fairly young and are used to sleeping in a cupboard but my husband and I are not. We booked a queen room expecting more room but no, the bed was under the window with only one side accessible so one of us had to clamber across to get to the other side. The en suite is part of the room so if you're sharing a room make sure you know them very well! On the positive side, there is free wifi, soft towels, tea and coffee, and the room is clean. I won't be staying there again.

title: Budget hotels could be done better
text: While I understand that this is a budget hotel and I have no problem with the room size there could be a few small additions to make ones stay easier. The addition of a mirror outside the bathroom near a power outlet would help people get ready as there isn't/can't be an outlet in the bathroom. If the window alcove had a shelf in it that would allow for better luggage storage. Some sort of shelves for night tables as there is nothing and more than 2 wall hooks. Aside from that be forewarned that the 1st day I paid for WiFi and was asked and given 4 codes for our 4 devices. At that time the pleasant front desk person told me that I would have to come down the next day as the codes expire every day (24hrs.). The next evening I asked a different front desk person for new codes as I was instructed. This rude employee told was unaware of my purchase and told me that as I already received 4 codes I received 1 more than I should have gotten. Be aware that it is apparently £10 for 3 days on 1 device. You are not paying for WiFi for the room but rather the device. Overall easyHotel a room to sleep and not much more which I am okay with. Given what I mentioned above along with the damaged hallway with a strong chemical smell I would not recommend this hotel.

title: Avoid, avoid, avoid and yup, avoid some more!
text: I don't think that there is anywhere on earth with worse staff. The two Australian staff members I encountered are the most unprofessional, racist/regionalist jobsworths I've unfortunately had to deal with. Zero common sense, unhelpful and lie to your face when you query rules etc. On top of that, the hostel is filthy with questionable 'security'. Don't be fooled by the hostels attempts to look all cool and fun on its instagram and Facebook accounts - that is sadly far, far from the reality. Save yourself the hassle and look elsewhere.

title: great budget accomodation
text: I very much like staying there. The location is perfect, close to the East End as well as Holborn. The breakfast is first class, the rooms clean and usually quiet. Bathrooms are shared, but I have not had a cue yet.

title: Having the zoo to yourself!
text: On holidays from Australia we booked this experience as a fun way to experience the zoo and have a different sleeping experience in London. The staff were extremely friendly and willing to meet our needs especially when my traveling companion wasn't feeling well and had stayed in the cabin, allowing us to bring him a doggy bag of dinner back for him. Feeding the animals at night was fun and waking up to a lions roar isn't something you would expect to experience in the middle of London! Yes it is expensive... but hey we were on holidays!

title: It gets the job done
text: I booked this room due to its location – which is great. The bed wasn't the best bed I slept on but nothing to complain about. It was a small room, again nothing too bad there. The room was old, but was overall nice. The issues I had were this: 1. Wifi – When we checked in, we were told that they had two wifi networks, free to use. This was great because I had a project to work on for that night. However when we tried to sign on, we could get no connection. It wasn't until our last night there that we were finally able to get any type of connection. 2. Breakfast Deposit – When they checked in, they took £20 off my card for a "breakfast deposit" in case we were to eat at the hotel. I specifically chose the package I did to avoid paying for breakfast because I knew that I wouldn't need it. They never refunded my card or mentioned anything about it. I was ripped off £20 (plus more because of the fees on my card for international usage).

title: Location is the best thing everything else is poor
text: Location to Paddington and Hyde park great and that's it! Booked as a last minute secret hotel, and I can safely say that had this not been a top secret hotel we'd have never booked it! The cost at £150 would have got us a lot more else where, the room was up 2 flights of stairs, the 1st was acceptable the second set I can only describe as stairs you'd have going to a budget attics conversion. The room was small, bed may have been firm a decade ago, and the bathroom, you could sit on the toilet and actually put your head in the sink they where so close together. In need of a lot of renovation as looking very tired and dated now.

title: Great stay!
text: Stayed at the morgan for two nights. Great location only a 5 minute walk to the Holborn tube station-which has a big Sainsbury next door. My luggage was delayed and was delivered to the hotel when i was out, the staff took the delivery and was ready for me when i returned to the house. I had a heavy suitcase and was assisted with it both during check in and check out. The breakfast was filling and adeqaurte, the morgan is definately recommended to those who are looking to stay in central london withouth busting their budget.

title: Staying for business or lisure, best location ever in London
text: Excellent location, less than 50 meters from oxford street. and marble arch station. Excellent breakfast variety, and very good Indian restaurant menu. Rooms have a catch, those on the inner court are very small, dark and clostrophobic, those on the main street are very good, Suites are super comfortable.

title: Room got burglarized
text: Stayed here for 2 nights before my room was broken into. They said this has happened before and honestly I don’t see how it hasn’t happened more. They don’t protect the building. You should have people show you their key cards when entering. The policeman showed up hours after I had left and supposedly the cameras “weren’t working” but my room was the only one broken into. Manager wasn’t very cooperative or sympathetic to my situation. Staying here would be a mistake. I would advise against it. I almost feel like it was an inside job

title: real british
text: It's my first time. Fantastic experience ! Great atmosphere, good price. Very good location, just opposite the tube station., and very closed to south bank bars and pub. Nice crowd in the pub, very polite staff. The hotel offer a very good english breakfast. The single room to much little.

title: Great location, great deal
text: I stayed here on the last night of my trip. I was flying out the next morning but didn't want to pay a ton of money to stay in the airport hotel. This place was perfect. It's literally right around the corner from the Paddington Station so getting to the airport was a breeze. The staff was very friendly and accommodating. I would stay here again.

title: What a dump
text: It was actually quite funny when I told my friends there were mouse traps in my room. Then I thought, Jesus, really. What a dump, the room was smelly, the lighting was terrible. Will never stay again!

title: Excellent for our purposes
text: We booked this hotel for its location which was easy cycling distance from the Olympic stadium as I was participating in the prudential ride 100. We arrived very late which wasn't a problem as they are open 24 hours and the chap on reception was brilliant. He said we could drive in and find a car park space and leave the van there throughout our stay. It cost £10 a night which I think is great value especially as it has a barrier and cctv and is just below reception. I was nervous beforehand as we had very expensive kit in the van but I slept well knowing all was safe. It was 11 at night and travelling up from Devon we are hungry and although the hotel bar was open they were not serving food. However the receptionist called a local restaurant for us to check their times or suggested a takeaway. He them produced a load of takeaway menus mentioning we could have them dilivered to the hotel where we were welcome to have in our room or eat in the bar. He even offered to ring and order them for us. He then very helpfully printed us off maps and gave directions. Honestly the service this member of staff gave us was 5 star - he deserves a pay rise. The room was very comfortable, had all we needed, was very clean and we could even see the Olympic park red tower from our window. We even took our bikes up to our room on the 2nd night and we saw other cyclists doing the same and the hotel didn't seem to mind. So all good so far but there is always a but! Just be warned there is a redo mix plant next door which can be a little noisy and the neighbours decided to have a rave in the warehouse next door too so this did disturb us a little but not the hotels fault. The only real down side is the breakfast. I'll be honest it is one of the worst breakfast experiences we have had. The breakfast room was busy and the empty tables were full of dirty breakfast dishes. We had to sit with other peoples breakfast crockery full of uneaten breakfast. The person who was clearing up certainly needs some training and a rocket put up her Peru vial as she clearly uninterested in her job and working at a snails pace. The food was also tasteless with a very limited choice. Cooked breakfast consisted of cheap sausages that didn't look cooked, baked beans and fake scrambled egg. No bacon or other cooked food on offer. I feel this is unacceptable holiday inn. Three items of cooked food only! Come on. Also most other items were running out like pastries and not replemished and the whole area was disgusting with food everywhere. Really someone needs to be keeping this area clean. This was a real shame as the staff on reception were so good but the breakfast staff need some help and you need to look at your quality of food. Overall I did enjoy staying here and I would stay here again, I'd just go out for breakfast.

title: Nothing to shout about...
text: Stayed for a weekend trip to London. The first room they provided was little more than a box and to be fair after a complaint the staff who were very helpful moved us to a slightly bigger room. Although the price was reasonable for "London" we were paying a lot and would expect better. For example the cleanliness and quality of the room was not up to scratch (toilet not cleaned and hairs found on the bedding) and the breakfast was below average. The bonus is that this is a central location, but if you are paying over £130 a night you would want better.

title: Excellent accomodation, exceed my expectations!
text: My and my friend stayed in Passfield hall for 3 nights in July and one night in August. Our room was spacious with comfortable bed and the sink in our room made all the difference! We had to share the bathroom with 2 other guests, but the bathroom is just next to our room and is always clean. The neighbourhood is quiet at night, but only a short walk (about 5 minutes) from Euston Station, and it is safe and not scary for girls to walk at night. The breakfast is great, a range of food to choose from and the portion is enough to last until lunch or even tea time! REMEMBER to request a room on the ground floor if you are travelling with large luggages, me and my friend had to drag our luggages (30kg each!) to the 4th floor! Also, wifi is not free, had to queue up to use the computer in the dining room or pay for the wifi plan.

title: Very Disappointing
text: A strange set up with the hotel reception in a different hotel a couple of doors away. The hotel was chosen for its location and the double room was reserved 5 months prior to our stay, our excitement on arrival soon turned to disappointment when we entered the room to see twin beds waiting for us. Although the room was clean, there was no soap or shower gel in the bathroom... When we asked about changing rooms we were informed they were fully booked, and the person on reception started looking through desk drawers in the hope that some soap might appear....hilarious really!! Thanks, but no thanks...look elsewhere!

title: Great location, wonderful people, good breakfast
text: Really great value for your money. Personal is super nice. Breakfast was better than I expected, good variety. Location is amazing. No lift was inconvenient when bringing bags to the top floors... Overall very good experience. Would stay again and recommend others :)

title: Overnight brief stay
text: If you look at the glossy photos on Bookings.com (the ones Pasha have put up) you'd think you were getting deal of the century. But glossy photos don't transfer here. 3 flights of steep stairs. Grubby carpets...TINY rooms and nothing like the photos. Dirty walls. More hanging space than Johnny Depp's bedroom but why? Tiny bed, dirty 2nd pillow. No curtains unless you call a net curtain a curtain! Right next to a train track!!! Luke warm water. Cold shower full of damp. Basically the worst £62 i have ever spent. Paint and caroet cleaning could go a long way

title: Awful hotel
text: Me and my wife booked this hotel as we were attending the nearby tabernacle notting hill for a gig. We arrived quite late so checked in without really seeing the room or hotel the staff were friendly. When we got back to the room later we were shocked it was dated but worse than that it was dirty. We were considering leaving then. But stayed the night as it was late. Too make a bad situation worse the next morning I found a cockroach in the bathroom. Worse hotel I've ever stayed in.

title: business trip
text: Costing over £650 for 3 nights, this 4 star??? hotel certainly disappoints. Rooms are small and barely furnished and the bathroom was so minute you could hardly get into it. WiFi was chargeable!!! - ridiculous given the cost of the rooms.. I left the hotel and returned home to discover my i phone charger had been left behind - when I rang they said it was not handed in by cleaning staff!!?? suggest they need to have a word about this as I definitely left it there.............. so be careful with belongings. Staff very indifferent and unhelpful in the main. will try to avoid this hotel in future

title: Bed Bugs!!!!
text: This hotel looked nice and wasn't daftly cheap, so i thought why not? I'll tell you why not. The sink and shower were both broken on arrival, the heating was stuck on, so the room was roasting! The breakfast consisted of 2 toast, 2 slices od processed cheese and a boled egg

title: Snug but groovy !
text: Stayed here for JUST one night at the end of a trip, and loved it.. VERY compact rooms, so pack light !, but once you're in the groove of the small design, you'll love it. There are rooms without a window, but that could be very claustrophobic, so suggest opting for a windowed room. covent garden is about 15 mins walk, and on a weekend, you'll feel that its a bit quiet here, but dont worry about that, just wear comfy shoes.

title: Excellent Service
text: We are staying at this hotel. Good location, good view and excellent service. Fast food shops, supermarkets, petrol station, Transport for London's Underground and National Rail's Station, Bus Station are all within 3-5 minutes walking distance.

title: Very good for the price
text: I stayed one night at The hanover hotel.The good points the place is decorated really nice colour schemes. The rooms was a little on the small side but it was clean and really good value for money. We had a triple room and I really can't complain. We had breakfast it was simple but that's all you need on a short break. The hotel was close to Wicked threate and BIlly ELliott. When we check out of the hotel we said bye to the member of staff on the reception and he didn't say any thing back.which I didn't think it was good customer service. I would stay at this hotel again if your a budget this is a great hotel

title: Lovely
text: Ive travelled quite a lot and this is one of the nicest backpackers Ive stayed at. Ive much appreciated the welcoming staff and the free safe. The garden was lovely too. The location was perfect for me as I used to work and live in west ken but also being next to the piccadilly line is very handy. See you next time!

title: don't sleep there unless you like bed bugs
text: We stay in this hotel for ten days on September 2009 and it was horrible. They didn't change the sheets and they didn't clean the bathroom. We noticed red spots on our skin and we thought that was from mosquitoes bites and day after day the spots became biger and increased. My husbant is allergic to insect bites and finely we went to the hospital in Paddington and the doctor informed as that many people have visited the hospital for the same reason. BED BUG

title: Long Weekend in London
text: We came down to London for a trip on the Orient Express as well as the London Eye, a tour of the Houses of Parliament and to see the West End Show 'We will Rock You'. The hotel was only a short walk from Victoria Station where we caught the train. Reception was very friendly, efficient and competant. All rooms and areas of the hotel were very clean and in excellant decorative condition. We did not know that there was only a continental breakfast and not a full english breakfast until we arrived at the hotel. On two mornings there was a shortage of milk and they had to send out for it and on the first morning they ran out of orange juice. The hotel appeared to be full and very busy but we would definately use it again in particular du to its excellant position.

title: OK hotel
text: Room was okay, good location, but breakfast is kind of chaotic and not that much to choose from. We were waiting for over half an hour on one of the days to get our breakfast served.

title: Disappointing
text: Initial impressions were good - excellent location with helpful and efficient staff on the front desk. The room , however , was a let down - dark , with a small double bed and cramped bathroom ( although the shower and toiletries were good ). Perhaps I was unlucky , but the lower ground floor facing onto the street was particularly noisy both from passers by and heavy vehicles whose engines running as they waited in the street set things vibrating in the room. Breakfast was included in my rate , but small plates for the buffet ( too small for toast , scrambled egg and a hash brown ) and a single cup of coffee seemed mean with much better value available nearby.

title: Can it get worse?
text: Apart from the very polite and friendly lady who checked me in there was nothing I liked about this place. They say rooms ready from 12.00. Not the case. I was put in a box on the ground floor very close to reception and the kitchen. The door was made of plywood with a 1970's lock. The bathroom was like something I once experienced in the USSR. You couldn't sit on the loo as the toilet roll holder was in the way. The noise from the corridor was unbearable. I popped by head into the restaurant for breakfast and decided to leave immediately for somewhere more decent. And to have been charged £100 for this experience was simply rubbing salt in the wound!

title: Nice, and convenient location
text: A great location, very close to Baker Street underground. Nice, clean room (if a little compact), and friendly professional staff. Air conditioning and decent WiFi add to the package :) The room was also quiet even though it was on a main road.

title: Perfect for a romantic getaway
text: The Portobello is a small boutique hotel, perfect for a romantic getaway. We got room 16 which was really lovely. Lots of space, great garden view and amazing four poster bed. The bathroom is tiny, really tiny. But there's a wonderful tub outside of it. The breakfast's croissants are delicious and service is very attentive. Lots of nice restaurants very close to it and Portobello road is steps away. Not a place I would go with kids but definitely a great choice for couples.

title: Nice
text: Staff are so lovely, breakfast was basic but filled us up til lunchtime. Room and bathroom were both tiny but we paid £100 a night so you get what you pay for. It was very central, underground was 5 mins away and there are some really nice pubs and restaurants if you venture off the Main Street. Only issue was dust on lockers and top of wardrobe! All in all it was fine for a 3 night stay in London 👍

title: perfect
text: this place is perfect in every way, the staff is very nice and accommodating, the concierge is well-trained, the food is delicious, the rooms are very luxurious with attention to detail. the beds were comfortable and softest

title: Unfunny Fawlty Towers
text: Arrived 11am Sunday, rooms weren't ready as to be expected. Checking in was extremely difficult and took an age with the check in assistant trying to retrieve our booking. We had suitcases with us which they offered to keep in storage so we could explore London. The staff kindly offered to take these to the rooms when they were ready, I tried to explain that there was 4 of us, so 2 different rooms so it may be wise to write on the labels which room each item of luggage needed to go....which I gave up explaining after 5 minutes. We then arrived back at the hotel in the evening, went to the room....no luggage!! We then had to go back down stairs to reception to ask for our luggage, which we were greeted with a totally blank expression. After numerous phone calls by the receptionist and 15 minutes of waiting our luggage finally arrived. There was no offer to help take these items to the rooms. The rooms were the smallest I've seen anywhere, very dated, cracked tiles in the bathroom, windows were secondary glazed so were unable to be opened and generally run down. On a positive note they were very clean. The service from start to finish was poor and totally bizarre, the hotel was run down and in urgent need of refurbishment. Would never return.

title: Never again - nothing like the website
text: The Hotel looks very "boutique" on the website. in reality the fittings are of low quality, table wobbles, towel rail and shelf in the bathroom is loose. we were unaware that the hotel would not be manned (normally Hotels with "Do it yourself check in are MUCH cheaper eg £50-£80 not £240. On arrival the automatic check in machine did not have a record of our booking. We telephoned the chap who tried to check us in, finally acknowledging that the machine could not let us in. we waited 10 minutes for a charming young lady to arrive and attend to another guest who was concerned about parking. The young lady spent 10 minutes with her showing her the Marks and Spencer Car Park. After 20 minutes we were shown in to room 3 (not our room) then into room 1. the shower did not work. I telephoned the chap again and explained that we were tired and so far our experience of onesixtwo was terrible and i felt like leaving! He told me to do just that! finally getting the shower to work we left to walk to Blackheath. We dcided to check the front door key. It did not work. We called the chap again who was most unhelpful. Fortunately at this point your sister in law arrived and told the chap that the key did not work. She tried her best to recover the terrible situation. In summary 1) The hotel is * star in reality and it is represented as **** on the internet and in price (The Clarendon hotel in Blackheath had vacancies at the same price with a car park/ staff/ quality fixtures and keys and showers that work, my error of judgement to choose 162 over the Clarendon) 2) The check in procedure was akin to a Travel lodge @ £80 ish not £240.00. It took 20 minutes to get to our room 3) the man at the end of the phone is short, rude and unhelpful. 4)your sister in law was very charming and tried her best to recover the situation. All in all it was the most horrific and disappointing Hotel experience I have ever had and i have spent the last 30 years travelling both at home and internationally on all budget levels *** to ***** star.

title: Afternoon Tea at Number sixteen
text: This afternoon tea was amazing! Excellent sandwiches, scones, and pastries. The place was very beautiful and service ''5 stars''. Possibility to have vegetarian sandwiches on demand. 20 pounds per person only! Good to know: the water is charged (5 pounds for the bottle).

title: Very comfy beds, awesome location for Olympia
text: Stayed here when visiting a 2-day event at the London Olympia. Great service at reception, nice clean and modern rooms and a huge comfy double bed with air con. I was actually amazed just how close it is to the olympia. Literally a 5 min walk and a single right turn. Would definitely stay there again. I didn't eat breakfast there, but it was great value at just shy of £8. You'd easily spend that at a local cafe or patisserie. Complimentary tea, coffee, water and biscuits in the room too which is a nice touch considering the value.

title: DONT
text: on the morning of my travel i got an email to state there was no reception, but have to walk around 5 minutes to pick up key.on my visit the family room was the attic 4 flights up, not good for family,property needs upgraded, no wifi working,shower NO hot water toilet basin in need of repair.on returning the key to pick up area, i told staff of my position, but sorry about that was not good enough no refund or discount, i wont return, sorry

title: Shame the people let the room down
text: The booking service for these apartments kind of ruined these for me. I booked them for a work conference and chose them on location. I was booking two apartments and felt they were the best option. The day before travel I had only received entry details for one room so I called to check. Found out that there had been a mistake and they had overbooked so the second room was in a different location. The only thing they could do was move both of us if we wanted to stay together. When we found the apartments which aren't really marked, my colleague was given a larger room, nice for her but not great for me! I felt that with the mistake both of us should have been upgraded. The apartment was nice however, but it was a hot day and the tech in the room wasn't working. Had to ask security to put the air con on as it was really hot. didn't work so had to go back and ask them again - turns out my room wasn't activated as occupied. None of the smart system worked at all so TV etc was pointless, as was the manuals! So although the apartment itself was nice, the overall experience,lack of acknowledgment from the company for being rubbish and the really long walk in the morning I would not book with these people again.

title: Absolute disgrace!!
text: If i was offered to stay in this place for free i wouldnt stay there!! Oh my god it was an absolute disgrace! It was filthy cramped and just a sheer let down at least for the price i paid anyway. Their website pictures shows luxury apartments and its no where near the standard they claim!! These pics will show you what ul get if u stay there!!

title: Terrible staff, will never return!!
text: As a member of the Accor group for 5 years, this has to be one of the worst experience. First check in, staff were not professional, 3 of them chit chatting in front of me while I stand there to check in. Room was a tiny box, the wall is that thin I could actually hear they guy next room heavy breathing, (not snoring). Then house keepers burst into the room at 7.30, while another one banging the wall with the Hoover at 8am!! Staff were not helpful throughout my stay!

title: Comfortable & Safe Hotel.
text: Enjoyed a comfortable 4 nights stay (8 to 12 June) at this hotel which is in a great location. The rooms (one single and one single deluxe) were clean and comfortable. The en-suite bathrooms are compact but modern and functional. The continental breakfast was of a good quality - consisted of fruit juices, packaged cereals, warm croissants, toast (Warburton bread), jam/marmalade/honey/butter spreads, fruit, tea and coffee. The manager (owner) was courteous, friendly and helpful - as were the staff. Some reviewers mention that the manager insists on no visitors to the rooms. The manager's explanation for this is to ensure the safety and well being of the hotel's guests and their possessions - I find this policy to be reassuring. The location is ideal for travelling across London - the following stations are within 2 minutes walk of the hotel: Shepherds Bus underground and overground railway station, Shepherds Bush Market overground Station and Goldhawk Road underground station. Westfield Shopping Centre (5 minutes walk) and Hammersmith shops (10 minutes walk) are close to the hotel. Nearby there are plenty of pubs and restaurants which serve a variety of lunches and evening meals. I will be returning to this hotel on my next visit to London.

title: Charming and Cheerful
text: Stayed at this delightful and characterful hotel on a "girls" trip to London and consistent with its sister hotels, it proved to be a real winner for service, style and comfort. The location is ideal for cultural activities as well as shopping. Easy access to theatreland via underground. Delicious breakfast with great variety. The garden is quite charming and an oasis of solitude. The staff are exceedingly helpful and professional. I was impressed with their enthusiasm and I felt like a really welcomed and valued guest. My room was immaculate and stylishly decorated. Well done yet again to this small hotel chain for providing an exemplary hotel experience!

title: Medically unsafe temperature on hot day and unbearable even after it cooled down outside
text: It's midnight and I'm currently in the room covering myself in cold water to prevent hyperthermia and wondering what to do. It was an unusually hot day when we arrived and the room, on the fifth of six floors felt noticeably hotter than the 93 degree outside temperature even with fan on and windows wide open as suggested by the very friendly but sweat drenched staff. We took cold showers and kept our children out of the room during the day but decided to stay because it looked like the temperature was due to drop to the 60s overnight, we had prepaid on Expedia so refund chances were iffy and everywhere else was booked up (Wimbledon week). Regretting that decision now. Still literally a sauna and we are a family that has travelled extensively on a budget in hot third world countries and normally don't complain about stuff. Otherwise small but clean room and good location. Utterly miserable right now. Avoid in hot weather at any cost

title: Amazing Stay!
text: Even the most seasoned of travelers will fall in love with this place. It got off to a great start as the staff went above and beyond to accommodate a special request I had made. It was very symbolic of their overall approach to customer service...they will do anything they can to make your stay more enjoyable. Great bathrooms/showers, comfortable beds, excellent location, a family atmosphere and so much more stood out during my time there. I would absolutely recommend staying here and am already looking forward to going back!

title: Oh My God!!! Was that a big mouse or a rat??
text: That was one of the worst hotels I have ever seen! The only good thing about it is the location and the fact that all the day you are out because you don't want to be in that hotel. Very old and smelly furniture. The rooms are very small, the windows are not secured and you get to hear strange noices wondering if it is some kind of mouse or a rat trying to find food! I don't think the bed sheets were clean either.

title: Very Nice
text: We enjoyed our stay at this hotel. We felt safe walking in the area. Our hotel was clean, staff friendly and amenities in the area included retaurants, pharmacy and grocery. would definitely stay there again!

title: Unusual kind of hotel for me but I would return
text: Recent reviews of this hotel have included one very critical review, so I'll say straight off that I am neither a friend of this hotel nor a member of staff, and of course every guest anywhere has their own opinion

title: Sakar Thank you for your hospitality
text: Me and my husband are regular to this hotel and every time we come gets better . From Sakar at the reception to the bell boy they all recognised us and breakfast staff are very friendly. Sakar all goes extra mile to make sure we have a perfect stay . This hotel is real home from home just because of Sakar's Hospitality.

title: Top notch & very friendly
text: We arrived later in the day but were welcomed by incredibly friendly staff. A nice room with good space and very nice bathroom. (Superb shower) The usual mini bar and amenities, even had straightening tongs. Prime location in Notting Hill which makes it very convenient for central London and easy access to all transport, The restaurant has room for improvement in the food department but the bar service and cocktails are really good, and made up for the short fallings of the food offering. I liked the lounge area as it had great attention to detail. I really liked all the artwork in the guests areas and bedroom, in all a great spot and would recommend this lovely London boutique hotel to anyone.

title: Excellent value and very convenient
text: We've used these apartments on a couple of occasions and always been very pleased with them. They are located just a few minutes from the centre of Greenwich so you have good access to the Tube, buses, the ferry to North Greenwich and the Emirates Cable car that runs over to the Excel centre. Greenwich village has a wide variety of restaurants, a big indoor market and of course a variety of local landmarks. The apartments are clean, quiet, well furnished and for anyone wanting to eat in they have a mini kitchen. Beneath the apartments is a Waitrose supermarket that opens long hours so buying and preparing meals is an easy option. There is secure onsite parking at reasonable daily rates if you want to ditch the car and travel round by public transport you can.

title: Not to repeat
text: If you dont have a electric jug clean dont leave it in the room. Terrible! dont offer your clients a dirt one with yellow water...Too much dust. A eiderdown makes a difference for such a cold city. The breakfast room was cold very cold.

title: A poor recommendation by Secret Escapes.
text: My wife and I booked an overnight stay on the recommendation of Secret Escapes. What a mistake! Neither the hotel or Secret Escapes warned us about an annex and it being across the road. This road is a 24 hour bus and taxi route and it wasn't that easy to cross. It was drizzling with rain and there no hotel umbrellas so we got soaked. Further we were not warned that there were no lifts and that the stairs were quite steep. I found them difficult to climb. Our room was small, tired, and not that clean. The shower door seal was coming off and there were unpleasant stains around the soap basket and shower tray. This is meant to be a no smoking hotel and yet we found two cigarette packets wedged between the wall and the bedhead on the far side of the bed. Obviously the room had not been thoroughly cleaned. The decor in our room, the stairway and hall were all 'down at heel' and needed refreshing. Breakfast was underwhelming. There was only one waitress who did her best but it took her nearly ten minutes to clear a table for us to use. We were greeted with one piece of cheese and one piece of ham on the cold plate, virtually no hot food in the heated trays, and a poor selection of fresh fruit. The coffee was bordering on the undrinkable. I cannot recommend this hotel and we will certainly never stay here again. I would question Secret Escapes decision to feature this hotel. The most concerning thing was that when we returned to our annex at 03:00 a.m. we found all the fire doors on every floor still wedged open. So much for the safety notice!

title: Lunch with friends
text: Casual lunch with friends. Food acceptable although bit on the pricey side for what it is. A quarter of rotisserie chicken including two sides around the £13 mark and the chicken was dry. Very welcoming, pleasant staff although I object to the practice of adding a £1 charitable donation on my behalf to the establishments charity of choice. If the Ship inn wish to give to charity they can do it from their profit, I prefer to chose when donating rather than it being done/ added to my bill without even asking. To clarify I do give to charity but when I chose to not when I’m eating out.

title: Great Hotel
text: Great for business or pleasure. Friendly staff with very clean and tidy rooms. Great showers too. Would recommend for short stay or long its not too far from the center of London and plenty of shops near by.

title: Awful!
text: Awful! We had booked and paid a room by internet and got a confirmation. However, when we arrived we were stuffed into a cab and brought somewere else (an inn further away). The cab driver told us that it happens all the time. The hourglass overbooks its rooms on purpose and you end up staying somewhere else (where there is no tube station around!). Nice doing business with you.

title: Save Yourself!
text: Left about midnight after killing the 11th bedbug and stayed on the cold Paddington Station streets for a few hours until I found a ride to Heathrow. The trains don't run until 5:30am. Thought about just staying in the room with the light on and exectuing the little buggers when they came out, but I noticed one crawling on my luggage and the idea I'd be taking them home decided it for me. The photos of blood on the sheets are I believe the residue of other executions. That's the way my sheets looked (but fresher blood, hopefully mine) when I left.

title: Overnight stay
text: Arrived at 11.30pm after a family wedding. Rooms cosy & functional - showers & bathroom clean. Staff friendly Breakfast was excellent, tasty and fresh. Overcharged when paid bill but rectified quickly and promptly.

title: Wonderful find...
text: Great hotel... love the building and the way it has been renovated keeping the original but updating by leaving bare floor boards and rustic bits with interesting colours and textures. Really clean , comfy bed and good breakfast- (just a slight bit off for that). The staff was really friendly and the neighbourhood where the hotel is, is out of rush and bustle of the more tourist areas and is residential- just a bit noisy though. We will stay again, as it is a short trip by train to any of the London attractions. And the price for a London hotel is really reasonable. Overall, highly recommended!

title: Cheap but poor
text: Great location, horrible small rooms, poor breakfast, but all at a great price. Close to the underground station and retail store. Wi-Fi not available at rooms for free, though there's a computer you can use in the lobby. Smoking area is actually a table on the street.

title: Not a good experience
text: This 'hotel' is unmanned, when the fire alarm went off one evening no one came to help us despite us calling several times. In the end we had to disconnect at the fuse. The toaster kept catching fire and the food ran out at breakfast. The bathroom was dirty and TV didn't work. I left something at the hotel which they confirmed they had found however despite sending 2 SAE (the first they didn't get) 5 weeks later and I still haven't been sent my belongings even though I have called several times to chase. I would not recommend this hotel under any circumstances.

title: Warning worst ever DO NOT stay
text: I don't normally post bad reviews I like to post positive but In all my years traveled staying in various places .. tents , caravans , hostels to 5* luxury our New Year's break was ruined with this appalling excuse for contemporary deluxe apartments.. we changed rooms 3 times so it's not as though it was a one off disgusting room 1st room was dirty filthy no sofa bed just a old rotten base and a stinky mattress Floor peeling away door frames filthy. Water coming up from the sink Changed rooms to a marginally cleaner room Went out for food came back for some sleep made cup of tea .. only thing in the fully equipped kitchen was a masher and chopping board !!!! Decided to go to bed ... sat on the bed and it collapsed 😡😡 looked under bed to see and all slates were broken (previously) and worse still filthy floor full of hair dust and just scum Moved again at 1am to one of the deluxe apartments beds were ok but again no equipment or cuttelry in kitchen Shower screen broken , sofa disgusting had to put a sheet on it to sit down And worse was the whole place smells of cigarettes the duvet pillows everything everywhere Apparently the manager wasn't happy with us ! Really ? I want a full refund 😡

title: Fine in the Med
text: WWas double booked elsewhere o had to find a hotel sharpish south of the Thames. Intenret led me here. Next dor to a very appealing chinese on the very mixed economy Old Kent Road. Good reception and service. Room the TV did not work so free Wifi was offered instead. My only real gripe was as the rooms having no carpet was very cold on the feet. Tiled floors are fine in the heat of the mediterreanean, but less so in the cool Autumn of England. Take some warm socks. Was abit noisy, but then this is London and somoene s busy building something somewhere.

title: Beaufort House
text: We spent a week staying in Beaufort House this year. We found the apartment spacious for a family of 5 only 2 streets away from Harrods and the Knightsbridge Tube station. The staff were extremely friendly and efficient, only too willing to help. The cleanliness throughout the building was always kept to a high standard. There are plenty of food outlets and pubs close by so it makes a great place to have as your base in London. For me the one item I found symbolised the attention to detail was the "welcome Basket" we found in our apartment on arrival. It contained enough essentials that you did not have to hurry down to the supermarket to buy breakfast cereal and milk. I can honestly recommend this establishment for a comfortable stay with all the mod cons

title: Don't stay here
text: When we came to our room (we just got the keys and walked alone to the last floor) we realized that the room wasn't cleaned from the guests before us, but we coudn't find any of the staff because it was late. Worst experience ever and I traveled the whole world. The smell was unbearable. There is no wi-fi in the rooms or at the reception.

title: A good night in Hackney
text: Easy walk from station. Good value, clean room, very comfy bed, helpful staff, friendly ambience if a bit noisy - but fair play it is a pub and I'm over 70! Great breakfast. Menu looked interesting but we were eating elsewhere.

title: Lovely little hotel
text: I booked this hotel last minute to go and watch a recent England game at Wembley, I was pleasantly surprised at how friendly the staff were towards me,which is very rare in London, my room was clean as was the rest of the hotel, it was a short 10 minute walk to the tube station or a 2 minute bus journey, about 5 minute walk to the town area where you have a wide choice of food and drink to chose from, all in all I would stay at this hotel when I make another trip to Wembley

title: Stale, requires a good shaking out.

title: Worst Hotel in Notting Hill
text: This hotel had many things wrong with it. First and foremost the Hotel staff were completely incompetent and unwilling to help or solve any of the problems we encountered on our stay. The top floor of the hotel suffered dreadfully from the stench of Sewage. The room did not have a window, and the plumbing in the room was awful and every time a tap was used or the toilet flushed the stench of sewage swamped not only the room, but the top floor as well. There was a constant noise wiring throughout the night which prevented us from sleeping. There was one thin bed sheet and no duvet provided and we stayed at the begging of November. The room did not even have the basic amenities, something you would expect for £90 a night. The continental breakfast consisted of a bowl of boiled eggs, a small container of cereal or the option of toast and Nutella – absolutely awful! When we complained to the hotel staff about the stench and the fact that we were quite possibly breathing in raw sewage the only answer we received was that there was nothing they could do - except hand over a bottle of 49p value bleach and cheap air freshener. They had no spare rooms and apparently knew of no other hotels in London in which to move us too and were unwilling to give us a refund or pay for another hotel room. After over half an hour of complaining and getting nowhere we had no other choice but to stay in the hotel room. The manger was apparently incognito and could not be contacted and coincidentally the ONLY member of staff authorised to make any sort of decision regarding everything.

title: Cheap yes...
text: I think we were not the only ones trying to have breakfast in the ridiculously small breakfast room (chairs piled back to back) who regretted our choice. Cheap in all ways. Unfriendly "staff", noisy and small rooms. Etc. Etc...At check-in, we were told to pay in cash or get an additional 30£ fee if we paid with credit card. What could be the reason for this? Choose a different hotel.

title: Fabulous hotel
text: We stayed here for 2 nights in a Junior suite. The room was lovely with bay windows opening out onto a balcony, it was very spacious and comfortable, the Queen size bed was comfortable, the sofa bed not so comfortable which is to be expected from a sofa bed. Tea and coffee is brought to your room anytime at your request, also scones and cream between 3 and 5pm. There is also help yourself beverages including alcohol between 3 and 11pm. Located in a great area, very safe, pretty, quiet and close to everything. Harrods is a short walk away and not far from the underground, a great base for sightseeing while in London. The staff were courteous and efficient. Our needs were always fulfilled immediately and with a smile. The wifi was patchy, my device dropped out constantly, luckily I didn't need to use the wifi for business so it did not affect me too much. If I were back in London I would definitely stay here again, we found the hotel comfortable and of a high standard.

title: Tiny, smelly rooms with even smaller bathrooms - you can find a better hotel!
text: The room we had was very small - a full size bed barely fit and the bathroom...what a joke! Imagine an airplane bathroom with a tiny shower. They keep your key when you leave - not sure why they insisted on this, but they did! You stand in a line for a breakfast that consists of toast and cereal in the smallest dining room I've ever seen! It was also very loud! The location was ideal, but there are tons of other options on the same road!

title: Beware - human beings in all their glory
text: For the first time in years, and because everywhere else seemed impossibly expensive on my dates, I chose a shared bathroom option. Never again. The contented comments on same, above, are beyond me,. Perhaps I shared time with a convention of Disgusting Human Beings, because most times I visited the toilet it had been left in a revolting condition. Perhaps if I had waited longer, the facilities might have been cleaned but unfortunately as one shares the floor with at least 6-8 other rooms (not the smaller number suggested above) one can't afford to wait! Also, as people were aware of queuing issues, many chose to shower at night and in the early hours. Being close to the bathroom was therefore a disaster, sleepwise. In addition, one of the DHBs above returned (from his convention?) at 4.30 a.m., shouting into his phone at top decibels. In this hotel one is inescapably close to fellow human beings in all their glory. The only plus is the location, obviously. The room itself was perfectly clean, if tiny. But sadly, never again.

title: student digs
